MetaMask adds Stellar integration, but cross-chain bridges require manual setup

The Oct. 29 rollout adds a Stellar address to existing multichain accounts, while receiving USDC requires funding and token activation.

By Gino Matos Reporter • CryptoSlate

01 MetaMask added Stellar to Mobile and Extension on Oct. 29, placing addresses in existing multichain accounts. 02 MetaMask’s documented flow needs at least 1 XLM initially, plus 0.5 XLM reserved for each token trustline. 03 MetaMask warns bridging without a trustline can lose funds, while ordinary Stellar sends without one fail. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

MetaMask added Stellar as a default network on Oct. 29, giving users a new route for stablecoin payments within the wallet.

Before an unfunded account can receive assets such as USDC through MetaMask's documented flow, it needs XLM funding and the receiving token activated.

The launch announcement says Stellar is live in MetaMask Mobile and Extension, with a Stellar address derived from the recovery phrase in existing users' multichain accounts. That brings the payments network into an account they already use, alongside assets on other networks.

Fund the account, then activate the token

MetaMask's Stellar instructions require a first deposit of at least 1 XLM for a new, unfunded address.

To prepare for USDC, users open Manage Tokens, enable the desired token, open its entry marked Inactive, choose Activate, and confirm the transaction. Merely adding the token to the visible list does not complete activation.

Related Reading Stellar activates Protocol 28 as network hits record throughput and RWA value climbs

Under Stellar's current reserve rules , an ordinary unsponsored account must maintain 1 XLM , plus another 0.5 XLM for each ordinary trustline. Other account entries can increase the minimum, and transaction fees need spendable XLM above the reserve. The locked balance remains in the account.

Stellar's network rules also allow another account to sponsor these reserves, including the base account reserve.

Users need spendable XLM to complete activation: the reserve increase and network fee cannot come from the amount already locked.

MetaMask users must fund a new Stellar account and activate a USDC trustline before receiving the token. A swap between tokens already on Stellar can automatically create a trustline in MetaMask. For a cross-chain swap into a non-XLM token, MetaMask requires the receiving trustline to be activated manually first.

MetaMask says it prompts users before bridge confirmation and warns that bridged funds can be lost if the trustline is missing when they arrive.

That warning differs from an ordinary Stellar token send to a recipient without the required trustline. In that case, MetaMask says the send fails.

posts.title: This Is What Binance Has Done Following $6.3B Hack
posts.titleVi: This Is What Binance Has Done Following $6.3B Hack
posts.summary: Binance co-CEO Richard Teng told the exchange’s customers that the company will cover all losses after a security incident estimated to have impacted $6.3 billion.
posts.summaryVi: Binance co-CEO Richard Teng told the exchange’s customers that the company will cover all losses after a security incident estimated to have impacted $6.3 billion.
posts.content:
Binance co-CEO Richard Teng told the exchange’s customers that the company will cover all losses after a security incident estimated to have impacted $6.3 billion.

Additionally, Binance has conceded that the compromised laptop, which was initially blamed for the breach, was not the only factor, as investigators have found additional points of attack.

In an X post, Teng said that the initial investigations suggested that an attacker may have gained access through a DevOps engineer’s compromised laptop, which allowed them to get into a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawals. However, he cautioned against reducing the incident to one employee’s permissions or a single click.

“To be clear: the attacker did not simply use one engineer’s permissions, and this was not a single “one-click” action,” the executive explained. “It involved a more complex attack process. Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual.”

Regarding what the exchange had done since the hack, the co-CEO pointed out that it had temporarily stopped withdrawals and had performed a complete security revamp of the whole withdrawal service and addresses connected to it. Binance also revoked the authorizations of affected addresses and has invited law enforcement agencies and on-chain intelligence firms to help trace and recover the money.

A later update from Binance changed the picture further, with the exchange saying subsequent investigations had uncovered “additional points of breach,” although it didn’t say exactly what they were.

Teng added that the company had found no evidence of a private key leak and that about $3 billion of the $6.3 billion that had been stolen had been frozen on-chain with the help of “blockchain partners.” Furthermore, he reiterated that customer funds were safe and that Binance will cover all losses from its SAFU fund as well as additional funds from the company.

Many X users responded positively to Teng’s explanation, praising the crypto firm’s “strong” leadership and transparency. Others were just relieved that their funds were safe.

However, some were less accommodating. One of them, the NFT account Chill Pill, which has a following just shy of 100,000, said it “wouldn’t trust Binance” at this point. Meanwhile, self-described crypto watchdog MASTR called the exchange incompetent and suggested that if it sold more assets to reimburse users, it could add pressure on the wider market.

Others, like former X head of product Nikita Bier, laid into Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao, calling him a “nomadic autistic man” and questioning his “funds are SAFU” response to the biggest crypto hack in history.

Indeed, the shock was felt in the market, with BTC briefly dipping to $76,300 and wiping out nearly $479 million in positions, with ETH recording another $363 million in liquidations.

The post This Is What Binance Has Done Following $6.3B Hack appeared first on CryptoPotato .

Written by Christina Comben staff editor Edited by Bryan O'Shea staff editor Written by Christina Comben staff editor Edited by Bryan O'Shea staff editor

Binance hackers raced to move billions before it could be frozen

Magazine Published Oct 30, 2026 Attackers raced to convert stolen stablecoins into crypto that issuers could not freeze as industry players like Tether and Circle moved to immobilize billions of dollars in assets.

Attackers behind Binance’s estimated $6.3 billion hack still control billions of dollars in stolen cryptocurrency despite efforts by token issuers to freeze the proceeds.

The attack, the largest in crypto history, began at 8:04 pm UTC Thursday and the perpetrators, linked to the same North Korean hackers behind last month’s Bitget hack, immediately began converting assets.

The game plan for the hackers was to convert the assets that could be frozen, like USDT and USDC, into ones that could not, such as Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH).

CertiK engineer Dickson Wu traced $500 million in USDT that was sent to one address, with $325 million sold to market makers for ETH by 20:59 UTC, less than an hour after the hack began.

They were racing against some of crypto’s most powerful gatekeepers: stablecoin giants like Tether and Circle, who had already begun blacklisting addresses associated with the theft .

Binance said Friday that about $3 billion of the stolen assets were frozen onchain out of an estimated $6.3 billion total, and that it is working with law enforcement , issuers and blockchain analytics firms to trace additional funds.

The scale of the theft is mind-boggling, even in crypto terms, but with around half of the assets already frozen, how much of the stolen crypto can the perpetrators actually spend?

Unlike BTC or ETH, which are decentralized cryptocurrencies with no central issuer and no one to hit the pause button, centralized stablecoins like Tether’s USDT and Circle’s USDC have issuers that can freeze tokens held at specific addresses.

Binance said it is working with law enforcement to trace the funds. Source: Binance

That gives them the power to act swiftly in incidents like these. Tether froze around $1.567 billion in USDT in total, with the first major freeze happening just 37 minutes after the stolen funds reached the attacker’s main Ethereum wallet.

Related: Binance says it holds $5B in matching tokens to cover hack losses

Circle froze around $823 million in USDC three minutes later, with other issuers like Ripple and World Liberty Financial following soon after.

The ability to immobilize crypto is not exclusively a stablecoin feature, and despite not having central issuers, some decentralized protocols like Arbitrum did not sit idly by.

Arbitrum’s Security Council moved around $30.5 million in ARB and ETH into an intermediary frozen wallet, where they can only be moved after further action by the council or a vote by Arbitrum DAO governance.

One important distinction remains — frozen funds don’t necessarily equate to recovered funds. Immobilizing assets prevents the suspected attackers from spending them, but it doesn’t automatically return them to Binance or its users.

Decentralized lending protocol Aave adds another layer of complexity to the equation. Between 20:58 and 21:01 UTC, a wallet associated with the attackers deposited $60 million in USDT into Aave V3 on Ethereum and borrowed $44.6 million of wrapped Ether (WETH), around 40 minutes before the first freeze.

LlamaRisk, an Aave risk service provider, said in its 1:00 am update that the attacker’s position subsequently held around $59.9 million in USDT collateral against $43.8 million in debt. Aave said the position remained overcollateralized and did not put protocol suppliers at risk.

Largest crypto heists of all time. Source: Elliptic

Since the USDT had already been deposited into Aave’s lending pool, blacklisting the attacker’s wallet could not automatically retrieve the collateral held by the protocol, as Aave Chan Initiative founder Marc Zeller explained :

To prevent further deposits and borrowing, Aave temporarily froze markets across its V3 and V4 deployments, although existing users could still withdraw funds, repay loans and liquidate positions.

Aave later lifted its precautionary freeze across V3 and V4 markets, saying its contracts were unaffected and positions remained overcollateralized.

“Just another day in crypto,” Zeller said.

Elliptic estimated that $2.84 billion had been frozen by 7:00 am UTC on Friday, while the attackers still controlled around $3.33 billion in assets that issuers could not immobilize.

And while the freeze almost halved the attackers’ profit pool, that doesn’t mean all the remaining funds are safe to recover.

Bitcoin and Ether don’t have a centralized token issuer that can blacklist individual addresses like Tether or Circle. So once stolen assets are converted into these native cryptocurrencies, transactions can be restricted, but freezing them is a lot harder.

Binance has pledged to cover all losses using its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and company funds, and says user assets remain safe; according to the latest update from Binance chief executive Richard Teng, the exchange is already “recovering stolen assets for users.”

The ability to immobilize crypto is not exclusively a stablecoin feature, and despite not having central issuers, some decentralized protocols like Arbitrum did not sit idly by.

Arbitrum’s Security Council moved around $30.5 million in ARB and ETH into an intermediary frozen wallet, where they can only be moved after further action by the council or a vote by Arbitrum DAO governance.

One important distinction remains — frozen funds don’t necessarily equate to recovered funds. Immobilizing assets prevents the suspected attackers from spending them, but it doesn’t automatically return them to Binance or its users.

Decentralized lending protocol Aave adds another layer of complexity to the equation. Between 20:58 and 21:01 UTC, a wallet associated with the attackers deposited $60 million in USDT into Aave V3 on Ethereum and borrowed $44.6 million of wrapped Ether (WETH), around 40 minutes before the first freeze.

LlamaRisk, an Aave risk service provider, said in its 1:00 am update that the attacker’s position subsequently held around $59.9 million in USDT collateral against $43.8 million in debt. Aave said the position remained overcollateralized and did not put protocol suppliers at risk.

Largest crypto heists of all time. Source: Elliptic

Since the USDT had already been deposited into Aave’s lending pool, blacklisting the attacker’s wallet could not automatically retrieve the collateral held by the protocol, as Aave Chan Initiative founder Marc Zeller explained :

To prevent further deposits and borrowing, Aave temporarily froze markets across its V3 and V4 deployments, although existing users could still withdraw funds, repay loans and liquidate positions.

Aave later lifted its precautionary freeze across V3 and V4 markets, saying its contracts were unaffected and positions remained overcollateralized.

“Just another day in crypto,” Zeller said.

Elliptic estimated that $2.84 billion had been frozen by 7:00 am UTC on Friday, while the attackers still controlled around $3.33 billion in assets that issuers could not immobilize.

And while the freeze almost halved the attackers’ profit pool, that doesn’t mean all the remaining funds are safe to recover.

Bitcoin and Ether don’t have a centralized token issuer that can blacklist individual addresses like Tether or Circle. So once stolen assets are converted into these native cryptocurrencies, transactions can be restricted, but freezing them is a lot harder.

Binance has pledged to cover all losses using its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and company funds, and says user assets remain safe; according to the latest update from Binance chief executive Richard Teng, the exchange is already “recovering stolen assets for users.”

Uniswap launches TJAR fee tool, but only fast searchers capture the hidden arbitrage profit

Uniswap says Robinhood uses TJAR for stablecoin fee receipts, while the chosen release price shapes outside traders’ surplus.

By Gino Matos Reporter • CryptoSlate

01 Uniswap says Robinhood already receives Uniswap API fees in USDC and USDG through its TJAR converter. 02 Outside searchers pay a fixed token amount for selected fee assets, seeking surplus after execution costs. 03 Lower release thresholds can accelerate receipts but leave more value for searchers when large fee deposits arrive. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Uniswap outlined on Oct. 30 how its Token Jar (TJAR) fee converter lets outside traders buy accumulated fee tokens for a fixed payment.

Uniswap opened TJAR to other apps on Oct. 29 , saying Robinhood already uses the system for fees collected through the Uniswap API across its supported chains and receives USDC and USDG.

Those stablecoin receipts come from traders known as searchers, who exchange the required payment for fee assets held in an on-chain Token Jar. The arrangement sends the chosen token to a configured destination while leaving searchers to assess whether the assets are worth taking.

A Token Jar holds incoming assets, while a Releaser contract specifies the payment token, amount, and destination. The app’s operator chooses those terms.

Related Reading Uniswap adds seven trading sources as 0x disputes its protection from malicious hooks

The developer documentation says a searcher pays the full release amount even when selecting only some assets, and receives the entire balance of each asset it names. Anything unselected remains in the jar, and the payment goes to the operator’s configured recipient.

The jar does not value its holdings, and no price oracle automatically adjusts the payment, so asset balances and market prices can change while that amount stays fixed.

Searchers have an incentive to act when the recoverable value exceeds the payment and execution costs. Competition can narrow that margin, but the mechanism does not guarantee a profit.

TJAR lets operators set a fixed fee for portfolio changes, while searchers keep the recovered value above payment and costs. Robinhood’s stablecoin setup differs from Uniswap’s protocol-fee deployment, which uses UNI sent to a burn address. TJAR lets other operators choose their destination.

The documentation currently says TJAR’s optional protocol fee is unset, although the Uniswap DAO controls that parameter.

Uniswap's faster receipts have a trade-off

Uniswap’s Oct. 30 pricing explanation says a lower release threshold generally lets jars clear more frequently, shortening exposure to token-price movements. However, a large deposit can suddenly push the holdings well above the fixed payment.

Its hypothetical example starts with a jar holding $950 of assets and a release price of 1,000 USDC. A $500 fee deposit takes the holdings to $1,450 without changing that price, so the resulting gap can reward the searcher at the operator’s expense.

A higher threshold makes individual deposits less significant relative to the payment, but generally leaves assets waiting longer before conversion. The operator balances frequent receipts against price exposure and the surplus available to searchers.

Decrypt News Law and Order Binance Hack Shows Why Offshore Exchanges Need US Oversight, CFTC Chair Says

Michael Selig said the record $6.4 billion theft shows why offshore exchanges should register with the CFTC and adopt U.S.-grade cybersecurity standards.

By Decrypt Staff Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

CFTC Chairman Michael Selig. Image: U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission/Decrypt

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

CFTC Chairman Michael Selig told CNBC the $6.4 billion Binance hack “proves our exact point” for the crypto-market rules the agency proposed this month.

Selig characterized the attack as a laptop-introduced vulnerability rather than a blockchain flaw—but Binance has since found “additional points of breach.”

The CFTC chair cast on-chain traceability as a regulatory advantage.

The record-breaking hack of Binance is exactly why offshore crypto exchanges need U.S. oversight, CFTC Chairman Michael Selig argued, using the roughly $6.4 billion theft to press the agency’s case for a federal rulebook.

Speaking to CNBC on Friday , Selig said the breach “proves our exact point” behind the crypto-market regulations the agency proposed earlier this month.

“The real issue here is that these are unregulated offshore exchanges, and they don’t have the same sorts of safeguards that we have in our financial markets here in the United States,” he said, pitching a “federal option” that would let such venues register with the CFTC and submit to the same cybersecurity standards that govern U.S. markets.

Selig sought to downplay the role of blockchain itself in the attack. The exploit, he said, didn’t break the underlying blockchain, in this case Ethereum, or its smart contracts, but exploited a vulnerability he believed was “introduced from someone’s laptop,” the kind of incident that happens in traditional markets too.

The difference with crypto, he said, is speed: funds can move far faster, and attackers can route them through tools like Tornado Cash to obscure their trail.

Selig’s characterization, though, may be incomplete. Binance initially pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, but said Friday that its investigation had since uncovered “ additional points of breach ,” with CEO Richard Teng calling it “a more complex attack process” that “did not simply use one engineer’s permissions.”

And while the theft did not expose a flaw in Ethereum itself, the attack did play out partly on-chain: The attacker used EIP-7702 , an Ethereum feature that lets ordinary wallets run smart-contract code, to turn a Binance hot wallet into a “sweeper” using 50 pre-signed authorizations, draining its assets.

TRM Labs said the broader breach points to a compromise of Binance’s signing infrastructure rather than a weakness in any blockchain.

Selig framed the blockchain’s transparency as a regulatory advantage regardless. “The fact that we can trace transactions on-chain, even when some of these technologies are used to obfuscate that, gives regulators a lot of potential to be really cop on the beat here,” he said.

The comments sharpen a pitch Selig has been making for weeks. The CFTC has pressed ahead with its own crypto rulemaking rather than wait on Congress, sending the White House proposals that would define event contracts as “swaps” and floating a plan to bring crypto exchanges under federal oversight , part of a broader shift in which regulators have taken the lead after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate.

The Binance hack hands that effort a vivid talking point.The exploit is the largest in crypto history, with Binance setting aside $6.34 billion to cover losses and assuring users their assets are safe. The Secret Service and FBI have opened a probe, and TRM Labs and Chainalysis have tied the theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group .

Decrypt News Law and Order Binance Hack Shows Why Offshore Exchanges Need US Oversight, CFTC Chair Says

Michael Selig said the record $6.4 billion theft shows why offshore exchanges should register with the CFTC and adopt U.S.-grade cybersecurity standards.

By Decrypt Staff Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

CFTC Chairman Michael Selig. Image: U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission/Decrypt

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

CFTC Chairman Michael Selig told CNBC the $6.4 billion Binance hack “proves our exact point” for the crypto-market rules the agency proposed this month.

Selig characterized the attack as a laptop-introduced vulnerability rather than a blockchain flaw—but Binance has since found “additional points of breach.”

The CFTC chair cast on-chain traceability as a regulatory advantage.

The record-breaking hack of Binance is exactly why offshore crypto exchanges need U.S. oversight, CFTC Chairman Michael Selig argued, using the roughly $6.4 billion theft to press the agency’s case for a federal rulebook.

Speaking to CNBC on Friday , Selig said the breach “proves our exact point” behind the crypto-market regulations the agency proposed earlier this month.

“The real issue here is that these are unregulated offshore exchanges, and they don’t have the same sorts of safeguards that we have in our financial markets here in the United States,” he said, pitching a “federal option” that would let such venues register with the CFTC and submit to the same cybersecurity standards that govern U.S. markets.

Selig sought to downplay the role of blockchain itself in the attack. The exploit, he said, didn’t break the underlying blockchain, in this case Ethereum, or its smart contracts, but exploited a vulnerability he believed was “introduced from someone’s laptop,” the kind of incident that happens in traditional markets too.

The difference with crypto, he said, is speed: funds can move far faster, and attackers can route them through tools like Tornado Cash to obscure their trail.

Selig’s characterization, though, may be incomplete. Binance initially pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, but said Friday that its investigation had since uncovered “ additional points of breach ,” with CEO Richard Teng calling it “a more complex attack process” that “did not simply use one engineer’s permissions.”

And while the theft did not expose a flaw in Ethereum itself, the attack did play out partly on-chain: The attacker used EIP-7702 , an Ethereum feature that lets ordinary wallets run smart-contract code, to turn a Binance hot wallet into a “sweeper” using 50 pre-signed authorizations, draining its assets.

TRM Labs said the broader breach points to a compromise of Binance’s signing infrastructure rather than a weakness in any blockchain.

Selig framed the blockchain’s transparency as a regulatory advantage regardless. “The fact that we can trace transactions on-chain, even when some of these technologies are used to obfuscate that, gives regulators a lot of potential to be really cop on the beat here,” he said.

The comments sharpen a pitch Selig has been making for weeks. The CFTC has pressed ahead with its own crypto rulemaking rather than wait on Congress, sending the White House proposals that would define event contracts as “swaps” and floating a plan to bring crypto exchanges under federal oversight , part of a broader shift in which regulators have taken the lead after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate.

The Binance hack hands that effort a vivid talking point.The exploit is the largest in crypto history, with Binance setting aside $6.34 billion to cover losses and assuring users their assets are safe. The Secret Service and FBI have opened a probe, and TRM Labs and Chainalysis have tied the theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group .

Decrypt News Markets Intel Stock Suffers Worst Crash in 50 Years as Weak Forecast Overshadows AI Chip Demand

Intel beat third-quarter earnings expectations, but warned of a prolonged PC slump, sending shares to their worst daily decline in 50 years.

By Jose Antonio Lanz Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Intel shares plunged nearly 30% to $65.76 on Friday, wiping out more than $146 billion in market value as investors reacted to a disappointing fourth-quarter forecast.

Intel expects Q4 revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, well below Wall Street's $17.07 billion estimate, while adjusted earnings per share are forecast at $0.25 versus expectations of $0.43.

Demand for AI server processors is booming, but manufacturing and packaging shortages are limiting production. Meanwhile, Intel expects the PC market to contract through 2027 and warned it probably won't generate positive free cash flow next year.

Intel shares plunged nearly 30% to $65.76 on Friday after the chipmaker issued a fourth-quarter forecast that fell well short of Wall Street expectations, overshadowing an otherwise strong earnings report.

The selloff wiped out more than $146 billion in market value, and translated into the worst single-day decline in more than 50 years.

The problem is that Intel finds itself in an unusual position: demand for its processors is booming because of the AI infrastructure buildout, but the company cannot manufacture enough chips to capitalize on it. At the same time, its traditional PC business is struggling, and the factories needed to support its long-term recovery are consuming enormous amounts of money.

Intel's third-quarter numbers were actually quite good. Revenue climbed 21% year over year to $16.5 billion, while adjusted earnings per share reached $0.52, beating the company's guidance of $0.38 and Wall Street's $0.40 estimate. It was the company's eighth consecutive quarter of exceeding its financial expectations, according to CFO Dave Zinsner.

The strongest performer was Intel's Data Center and AI division, which generated $7.3 billion in revenue, up 78% year over year and nearly 80% compared with the same period last year. The division's operating profit reached $3 billion, representing 42% of its revenue.

But investors were looking at what comes next. Intel expects fourth-quarter revenue between $15 billion and $16 billion, meaning its midpoint guidance of $15.5 billion is roughly $1.6 billion below the $17.07 billion analysts had anticipated. Adjusted earnings per share are expected to fall to $0.25, compared with Wall Street's $0.43 estimate.

Gross margins, which measure how much revenue remains after accounting for the direct costs of making products, are also expected to deteriorate. Intel forecast a non-GAAP gross margin of 38% for Q4, down from 44.1% in the third quarter.

Three problems explain much of that deterioration: weaker PC demand, manufacturing constraints affecting server processors, and an accident at one of Intel's factories in Israel.

Intel CFO Dave Zinsner described 2027 as an investment year and warned investors not to expect positive free cash flow. Free cash flow is the money a company has left after paying operating expenses and investments in equipment and infrastructure. Intel expects to sacrifice cash generation in the short term to finance its manufacturing expansion.

"Probably not a dynamic where we are going to have positive free cash flow next year," Zinsner said during the earnings call. He added that Intel expects a return on invested capital of at least 20% on its manufacturing node investments, but acknowledged that several major projects will require substantial spending at the same time.

That spending is part of Intel's broader attempt to rebuild its manufacturing business and compete with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, or TSMC, the world's leading contract chipmaker. Intel beat third-quarter earnings expectations, but warned of a prolonged PC slump, sending shares to their worst daily decline in 50 years.

By Jose Antonio Lanz Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Intel shares plunged nearly 30% to $65.76 on Friday, wiping out more than $146 billion in market value as investors reacted to a disappointing fourth-quarter forecast.

Intel expects Q4 revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, well below Wall Street's $17.07 billion estimate, while adjusted earnings per share are forecast at $0.25 versus expectations of $0.43.

Demand for AI server processors is booming, but manufacturing and packaging shortages are limiting production. Meanwhile, Intel expects the PC market to contract through 2027 and warned it probably won't generate positive free cash flow next year.

Intel shares plunged nearly 30% to $65.76 on Friday after the chipmaker issued a fourth-quarter forecast that fell well short of Wall Street expectations, overshadowing an otherwise strong earnings report.

The selloff wiped out more than $146 billion in market value, and translated into the worst single-day decline in more than 50 years.

The problem is that Intel finds itself in an unusual position: demand for its processors is booming because of the AI infrastructure buildout, but the company cannot manufacture enough chips to capitalize on it. At the same time, its traditional PC business is struggling, and the factories needed to support its long-term recovery are consuming enormous amounts of money.

Intel's third-quarter numbers were actually quite good. Revenue climbed 21% year over year to $16.5 billion, while adjusted earnings per share reached $0.52, beating the company's guidance of $0.38 and Wall Street's $0.40 estimate. It was the company's eighth consecutive quarter of exceeding its financial expectations, according to CFO Dave Zinsner.

The strongest performer was Intel's Data Center and AI division, which generated $7.3 billion in revenue, up 78% year over year and nearly 80% compared with the same period last year. The division's operating profit reached $3 billion, representing 42% of its revenue.

But investors were looking at what comes next. Intel expects fourth-quarter revenue between $15 billion and $16 billion, meaning its midpoint guidance of $15.5 billion is roughly $1.6 billion below the $17.07 billion analysts had anticipated. Adjusted earnings per share are expected to fall to $0.25, compared with Wall Street's $0.43 estimate.

Gross margins, which measure how much revenue remains after accounting for the direct costs of making products, are also expected to deteriorate. Intel forecast a non-GAAP gross margin of 38% for Q4, down from 44.1% in the third quarter.

Three problems explain much of that deterioration: weaker PC demand, manufacturing constraints affecting server processors, and an accident at one of Intel's factories in Israel.

Intel CFO Dave Zinsner described 2027 as an investment year and warned investors not to expect positive free cash flow. Free cash flow is the money a company has left after paying operating expenses and investments in equipment and infrastructure. Intel expects to sacrifice cash generation in the short term to finance its manufacturing expansion.

"Probably not a dynamic where we are going to have positive free cash flow next year," Zinsner said during the earnings call. He added that Intel expects a return on invested capital of at least 20% on its manufacturing node investments, but acknowledged that several major projects will require substantial spending at the same time.

That spending is part of Intel's broader attempt to rebuild its manufacturing business and compete with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, or TSMC, the world's leading contract chipmaker. Intel wants to manufacture chips not only for its own products but also for outside customers, a business model known as a foundry.

The turnaround has attracted major partners. In September 2025, Nvidia invested $5 billion in Intel and agreed to collaborate on custom processors for PCs and data centers. The partnership gave Intel a financial boost while connecting its processors to Nvidia's AI ecosystem.

Intel's next-generation 18A process, the manufacturing technology behind chips such as Panther Lake , is central to the company's attempt to regain its technological edge.

More recently, a preliminary agreement with Apple to manufacture some of its chips helped send Intel shares above $130 in May. The potential deal could give Intel a significant new customer as Apple looks to diversify its manufacturing supply chain.

Those developments helped fuel optimism around Intel's recovery, but Friday's selloff shows how much still needs to go right. The company has strong demand in its data center business, yet it must increase manufacturing output, navigate a shrinking PC market and finance an expensive expansion before investors can expect consistent cash generation.

posts.content:
The cryptocurrency market saw major volatility over the past week, with one altcoin hitting a brief record high before dropping sharply. The frog-themed meme coin PEPE also grabbed headlines, posting strong gains despite the broader market downturn, but the spotlight eventually shifted to Binance.

The biggest crypto exchange suffered a $6.3 billion hack, undermining the digital asset sector’s reputation and sparking panic across the community. Prior to that, the company said it would delist numerous trading pairs.

Earlier this week, Quack AI (Q) suddenly exploded to a new all-time high of $0.24, while its market capitalization surged to nearly $1 billion, making it one of the top 100 biggest cryptocurrencies. Nonetheless, the token quickly gave up its gains, collapsing back to around $0.06 and nearly returning to its pre-rally level.

While it remained unclear what triggered the classic “pump-and-dump” move, some savvy traders took advantage of the price action, sparking speculation that they had inside information.

Trader 0xF1fE profited almost $1 million mainly by opening long positions on Q as the price rose, while Crypto with Haris ₿ said he made over $17,000 after catching “the perfect top” to short Q.

The AI-related altcoin remained highly volatile in the following days and currently trades around $0.04, up 15% on a daily scale and down 60% on a weekly basis.

The popular meme coin has jumped by 6% over the past week and, as of this writing, is worth around $0.0000052. It boasts a market capitalization of around $2.2 billion, making it the 46th-biggest cryptocurrency.

The main reason for its strong performance is a recent move by TRON’s Justin Sun. Earlier this week, several sources reported that the Chinese businessman increased his PEPE holdings to 11.85 trillion coins, becoming the token’s largest individual holder. In fact, only Binance, Robinhood, and Coinbase own more PEPE than he does.

Analysts like Altcoin Sherpa and Sweep assumed that the meme coin’s uptrend isn’t over yet, while the X account BSCN recently revealed that one “legendary” whale has purchased more than 45 billion PEPE for roughly $206,000.

Undoubtedly, the top news of the week, and perhaps of the year so far, is the $6.3 billion hack that Binance suffered. Some suspect that the perpetrators are the North Korea-associated group TraderTraitor, which also stood behind the $1.5 billion attack on Bybit last year. If you are willing to learn more about the incident, take a look at our dedicated article here .

The hack negatively impacted the crypto sector and triggered about $1.5 billion in liquidations, most of which were long positions. In the aftermath, the industry’s total market capitalization dropped 3.6% over the past 24 hours to around $2.68 trillion.

This is a clear plunge, yet some might have expected a bigger catastrophe, given that Binance is a major symbol of the crypto world and remains the leader in its field. According to X user Quinten, the market didn’t crash more after the massive hack for one reason: “no domino effect.”

“Unlike FTX and other collapses, this won’t trigger a chain reaction of bankruptcies, liquidations and further losses across the industry. Money was stolen from the world’s biggest exchange. Binance has the funds to cover it. Nobody else takes the hit. Why would the market crash over an isolated incident involving the player with the deepest pockets in the industry? No contagion. No bankruptcy risk. No domino effect,” he explained.

Beyond the chaos with the multi-billion attack, Binance performed wallet maintenance on the ETH network on October 28, briefly suspending deposits and withdrawals on that blockchain. No complaints were raised, and operations should have resumed.

The company also said it will delist the following spot trading pairs: AAVE/BTC, ATOM/BTC, CAKE/BTC, DASH/BTC, ETC/BTC, ICP/BTC, PENDLE/BTC, RENDER/BTC, TAO/BTC, THETA/BTC, XAUT/BTC and XTZ/BTC and the margin trading pairs RE/USD1, 币安人生/U, KAT/U, BTC/USDS, ETH/USDS, AVNT/U, FET/U, TRUMP/U, APT/U, WLFI/U on October 30.

Dimitar got interested in cryptocurrencies back in 2018 amid the prolonged bear market. His biggest passion in the field is Bitcoin and he was fascinated with its journey. With a flair for producing high-quality content, he started covering the cryptocurrency space in late 2018. His hobby is football.

Binance hackers deploy never-seen-before laundering tactics to conceal $6.3 billion theft

Chainalysis uncovered thousands of suspected automated transfers, while Elliptic traced $786 million in stolen stablecoins converted into other cryptocurrencies.

By Oluwapelumi Adejumo Senior Reporter • CryptoSlate

01 Chainalysis uncovered previously unseen laundering patterns as Binance hackers moved stolen assets through thousands of suspected automated transactions. 02 Elliptic traced $786 million in stolen stablecoin conversions, with attackers accepting discounts of up to 26% to rapidly move funds. 03 Investigators now face complex wallet loops and repeated transfers, while 18,270 stolen BTC remain spread across 19 addresses. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Hackers behind Binance's $6.3 billion breach are using previously unseen laundering tactics while rapidly converting stolen assets into other cryptocurrencies.

On Oct. 30, blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis said that investigators identified thousands of transactions executed within short periods , suggesting the attackers used automation to obscure the movement of stolen funds.

The discovery comes as Elliptic reported that the hackers had converted a pproximately $786 million in stolen stablecoins into Ethereum and Tron before asset freezes took effect, sometimes accepting significant losses to complete transactions quickly.

Binance hackers use automated wallet loops and aggressive token swaps

According to Chainalysis , the attackers have adopted unusual transaction patterns that repeatedly circulate stolen assets among interconnected cryptocurrency addresses.

The funds sometimes return to wallets involved earlier in the laundering sequence , creating complicated transaction histories.

The firm described these movements as “laundering patterns we have not seen before,” pointing to their speed and repetitive nature as evidence of suspected automation.

A dense transaction network links hundreds of wallets through several highly connected addresses. Source: Chainalysis Investigators also identified a distinctive pattern on the Tron blockchain, where numerous wallets received exactly 1 TRX before accepting additional funds and forwarding them to other addresses.

Analysts at Cantor Fitzgerald, TD Cowen and Compass Point say the record $6.4 billion theft is a Binance security failure, not a crypto-wide threat, pointing clients toward proxies like Coinbase, Robinhood, and Strategy.

By Decrypt Staff Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Cantor Fitzgerald, TD Cowen and Compass Point told clients in Friday notes that the $6.4 billion Binance hack—the largest ever—is unlikely to derail crypto’s recovery, framing the selloff as a buying opportunity for crypto-linked stocks.

Cantor’s Ramsey El-Assal said “we would be buyers on weakness,” citing $3 billion in frozen funds; TD Cowen called it a Binance security issue, not a Bitcoin problem; Compass Point said Binance has “more than enough liquidity to cover the hole.”

Moody’s struck a more cautious note on hot-wallet and concentration risks.

Wall Street analysts are telling clients the record-breaking hack of Binance is a buying opportunity, not a reason to flee, urging investors to scoop up crypto-linked stocks while prices are depressed.

Analysts at Cantor Fitzgerald, TD Cowen, and Compass Point said in Friday research notes that the roughly $6.3 billion theft, the largest crypto hack ever, is unlikely to derail the broader market’s recovery.

The reassurance came a day after the exploit rattled markets and sent Bitcoin sliding toward $77,000.

Cantor’s Ramsey El-Assal pointed to how fast the industry moved to contain the damage, noting that stablecoin issuers and others froze roughly $3 billion of the stolen funds, with Tether freezing more than $1.5 billion, Circle about $800 million and Ripple around $200 million.

El-Assal expects shares of Coinbase, Robinhood, and Strategy to recover once the panic fades. “We would be buyers on weakness,” he wrote, adding that while the episode is painful, “this is not 2022.”

TD Cowen’s Lance Vitanza struck a similar note, arguing the breach exposed weaknesses in Binance’s own security rather than in the underlying technology behind Bitcoin, and framing the selloff as a chance to add to Bitcoin and the stocks of public companies that hold it.

Compass Point’s Ed Engel and Michael Donovan said Binance has “more than enough liquidity to cover the hole,” while flagging that reimbursing customers could strain stablecoin supply and that rivals like Coinbase and Hyperliquid could pick up business. They are watching the $75,000 to $77,000 Bitcoin range as a key level.

The logic behind buying stocks over tokens is that regulated, exchange-listed proxies like Coinbase, Robinhood, and Strategy offer crypto exposure without the custody risk the hack laid bare, and tend to rebound once sentiment steadies.

Not everyone is sanguine. Cristiano Ventricelli, vice president of digital assets at Moody’s Ratings, said the incident “underscores the heightened cybersecurity risks associated with hot wallets” and “illustrates the risk concentration inherent in large, centralized intermediaries.”

He cautioned that the broader implications will hinge on “the ultimate losses, affected counterparties, asset recovery, and importantly, whether the incident leads to wider disruption or loss of confidence.”

Binance has set aside $6.34 billion to cover losses and told users their assets are safe, while the Secret Service and FBI have opened a probe and firms including TRM and Chainalysis have tied the hack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group.

Decrypt News Business Worried About Crypto Hacks? Buy Bitcoin Proxies in Stock Market Instead, Say Wall Street Firms

Analysts at Cantor Fitzgerald, TD Cowen and Compass Point say the record $6.4 billion theft is a Binance security failure, not a crypto-wide threat, pointing clients toward proxies like Coinbase, Robinhood, and Strategy.

By Decrypt Staff Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Cantor Fitzgerald, TD Cowen and Compass Point told clients in Friday notes that the $6.4 billion Binance hack—the largest ever—is unlikely to derail crypto’s recovery, framing the selloff as a buying opportunity for crypto-linked stocks.

Cantor’s Ramsey El-Assal said “we would be buyers on weakness,” citing $3 billion in frozen funds; TD Cowen called it a Binance security issue, not a Bitcoin problem; Compass Point said Binance has “more than enough liquidity to cover the hole.”

Moody’s struck a more cautious note on hot-wallet and concentration risks.

Wall Street analysts are telling clients the record-breaking hack of Binance is a buying opportunity, not a reason to flee, urging investors to scoop up crypto-linked stocks while prices are depressed.

Analysts at Cantor Fitzgerald, TD Cowen, and Compass Point said in Friday research notes that the roughly $6.3 billion theft, the largest crypto hack ever, is unlikely to derail the broader market’s recovery.

The reassurance came a day after the exploit rattled markets and sent Bitcoin sliding toward $77,000.

Cantor’s Ramsey El-Assal pointed to how fast the industry moved to contain the damage, noting that stablecoin issuers and others froze roughly $3 billion of the stolen funds, with Tether freezing more than $1.5 billion, Circle about $800 million and Ripple around $200 million.

El-Assal expects shares of Coinbase, Robinhood, and Strategy to recover once the panic fades. “We would be buyers on weakness,” he wrote, adding that while the episode is painful, “this is not 2022.”

TD Cowen’s Lance Vitanza struck a similar note, arguing the breach exposed weaknesses in Binance’s own security rather than in the underlying technology behind Bitcoin, and framing the selloff as a chance to add to Bitcoin and the stocks of public companies that hold it.

Compass Point’s Ed Engel and Michael Donovan said Binance has “more than enough liquidity to cover the hole,” while flagging that reimbursing customers could strain stablecoin supply and that rivals like Coinbase and Hyperliquid could pick up business. They are watching the $75,000 to $77,000 Bitcoin range as a key level.

The logic behind buying stocks over tokens is that regulated, exchange-listed proxies like Coinbase, Robinhood, and Strategy offer crypto exposure without the custody risk the hack laid bare, and tend to rebound once sentiment steadies.

Not everyone is sanguine. Cristiano Ventricelli, vice president of digital assets at Moody’s Ratings, said the incident “underscores the heightened cybersecurity risks associated with hot wallets” and “illustrates the risk concentration inherent in large, centralized intermediaries.”

He cautioned that the broader implications will hinge on “the ultimate losses, affected counterparties, asset recovery, and importantly, whether the incident leads to wider disruption or loss of confidence.”

Binance has set aside $6.34 billion to cover losses and told users their assets are safe, while the Secret Service and FBI have opened a probe and firms including TRM and Chainalysis have tied the hack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group.

posts.content:
Binance gives 48-hour withdrawal target while Bitcoin deposits remain open

Binance’s target leaves crypto withdrawals pending, while its Japan business confirms that trading and fiat transfers work.

By Liam 'Akiba' Wright Editor-in-Chief • CryptoSlate

01 Trading can change Bitcoin exposure while a paused withdrawal route still prevents external transfers. 02 Binance Japan confirms normal deposits, trading and fiat transfers; crypto withdrawals remain paused. 03 Binance plans a reserve update after remediation; roughly $3 billion remains frozen pending recovery. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Binance withdrawals remain suspended while deposits operate normally, leaving Bitcoin holders able to send assets into its global platform without an available crypto withdrawal route out.

The exchange's Oct. 30 security update estimates the incident's total impact at around $6 billion. For a holder who wants Bitcoin in a personal wallet or on another venue, an exchange balance and a completed blockchain transfer are different outcomes.

Binance News reports an expectation that withdrawals will resume within 48 hours as the exchange overhauls the withdrawal service and related addresses. CryptoSlate's Oct. 30 report describes Binance's latest update as estimating resumption in 45 hours. These are reported restoration estimates; neither establishes a precise verified reopening time.

If the pause continues into the weekend, holders will face price changes while their outgoing transfer route remains closed. Their ability to respond depends on which services their own account can use.

Related Reading Binance hack began with a $296 million XRP drain after 36-hour preparation

Trading access while Binance withdrawals are paused

Binance Japan’s initial Oct. 30 notice showed how trading and transfer permissions could diverge. It said trading remained available while deposits and withdrawals of all crypto assets were temporarily suspended. The regional business reported no confirmed impact on its customer assets.

Where trading remains available, a customer may be able to sell Bitcoin or change the asset held in an exchange account. That changes market exposure; it does not, by itself, put assets into an external wallet.

Binance Japan subsequently reported normal crypto deposits, trading and fiat movements, while crypto withdrawals remained paused. The earlier notices had described a different position:

Global and Japan notices describe different deposit conditions. Binance's global update says deposits are normal; Japan's notice says its crypto deposits are suspended. Customers cannot apply one entity's announcement to the other or assume that an available trading screen establishes access to every product and transfer service.

In a later Oct. 30 update , Binance Japan said crypto deposits, trading, and fiat deposits and withdrawals were operating normally. Crypto withdrawals remained paused, with resumption expected within 48 hours. Those service confirmations apply to Binance Japan.

The 48-hour guidance is a restoration target during a security overhaul. It does not guarantee simultaneous reopening for every asset, network and account.

The pause in Binance withdrawals also constrains any arbitrage strategy that requires moving coins out of Binance. Arbitrage is the attempt to trade price differences between venues; a route that depends on a suspended withdrawal cannot be completed in the usual sequence.

Traders who already hold balances on more than one venue may have routes that do not require an immediate outgoing transfer from Binance.

CryptoSlate’s Bitcoin market data displayed BTC at $77,077 when checked at 13:48 UTC on Oct. 30.

Related Reading Bitcoin dives below $79,000 as Binance hot wallet drained by Tornado Cash-linked wallet

The US Bureau of Labor Statistics scheduled the third-quarter Employment Cost Index for 8:30 a.m. Eastern on Oct. 30, or 12:30 UTC. Its September release reported that civilian compensation costs rose 0.8% over the quarter, seasonally adjusted. The index measures changes in employer compensation costs, including wages, salaries and benefits.

Farside Investors’ completed Oct. 29 session shows $17 million in net Bitcoin ETF inflows. Its Oct. 30 row was still incomplete at review time.

Binance says approximately $3 billion in affected assets has been frozen on-chain through cooperation with blockchain partners. Frozen assets are not confirmed recovered funds or demonstrated customer withdrawal liquidity.

Related Reading Trump's crypto firm joins Tether, Circle, and Ripple in $2.6 billion stablecoin freeze as Binance hack outflows near $6 billion

The exchange also promises to cover losses using its SAFU fund and company funds, and to publish an updated proof of reserves after remediation.

For service access, the practical evidence would be a completed customer withdrawal, a corresponding blockchain transaction and receipt at the destination. Repeated successful transfers, alongside a clear official description of restored services, would support a broader reopening claim.

The promised reserve update answers a separate question about disclosed asset backing.

posts.content:
Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong and two other insiders filed Rule 10b5-1 plans that let them schedule share sales in advance, with potential sales starting in November 2026 and January 2027.

The filing covers up to 13.59 million Class A shares, and at the October 29 closing price of $160.59, they carry a notional value of about $2.18 billion.

According to the document deposited with the SEC, Armstrong adopted his plan on August 12, and it allows for the sale of as many as 8.1 million shares tied to the exercise of vested stock options, with transactions scheduled to kick off around November 16, 2026, and go on until October 22, 2027, subject to price thresholds in the arrangement.

The second insider looking to liquidate part of their holding is board member Frederick Ernest Ehrsam III, who entered into his plan on September 4. His covers up to 3.8 million Class A shares issuable when Class B shares held by his living trust are converted. Per the filing, the estimated start date is December 7, 2026, with an expiration date of June 7, 2027.

Emilie Choi, Coinbase’s president and chief operating officer, is the third insider mentioned in the document. She adopted her plan a few days after Ehrsam, and it covers the least number of shares of the three, at just over 1.5 million, including stock she owns as well as shares linked to equity awards and stock held by a trust for which her spouse is a co-trustee.

Her window is set to open around January 4, 2027, and closes on the very last day of that year.

The Rule 10b5-1 filing coincided with Coinbase releasing its Q3 2026 results that showed a net income of $719 million, or $2.51 per share, compared to $432.6 million ($1.50 per share) a year earlier.

Transaction revenue went down by 43% to just over $590 million, when last year it had reached $1.05 billion, with prediction markets emerging as a huge growth area for the firm, bringing in more than $200 million in revenue. That area, combined with derivatives, accounted for at least 25% of Coinbase’s total transaction revenue, with subscriptions and services making up 49%.

Additionally, the results showed that total operating expenses between July and September dropped by 17% to $1.15 billion, where it had been about $1.39 billion in the same period in 2025.

Meanwhile, the company’s COIN stock closed yesterday at $160.59 but fell almost 5% to $152.98 in after-hours trading. And as we reported yesterday, the Coinbase stock has fallen by at least 56% from its recent peak, placing it among the weakest performers in a group of major technology companies.

His passion for understanding financial systems has led to an intriguing interest in blockchain technology, and he enjoys exploring and writing about cryptocurrencies. Possessing a keen intellect and diligent work ethic, he stays up-to-date on the latest industry trends, regularly sharing his insights in articles and professional presentations.

The Rule 10b5-1 filing coincided with Coinbase releasing its Q3 2026 results that showed a net income of $719 million, or $2.51 per share, compared to $432.6 million ($1.50 per share) a year earlier.

Transaction revenue went down by 43% to just over $590 million, when last year it had reached $1.05 billion, with prediction markets emerging as a huge growth area for the firm, bringing in more than $200 million in revenue. That area, combined with derivatives, accounted for at least 25% of Coinbase’s total transaction revenue, with subscriptions and services making up 49%.

Additionally, the results showed that total operating expenses between July and September dropped by 17% to $1.15 billion, where it had been about $1.39 billion in the same period in 2025.

Meanwhile, the company’s COIN stock closed yesterday at $160.59 but fell almost 5% to $152.98 in after-hours trading. And as we reported yesterday, the Coinbase stock has fallen by at least 56% from its recent peak, placing it among the weakest performers in a group of major technology companies.

Tether’s excess reserves nearly double to $8B as Q3 profit hits $1.5B

Latest News Published Oct 30, 2026 The stablecoin issuer’s US Treasury holdings are comparable to those of major foreign holders, while its Bitcoin reserves were valued at $8.37 billion at the end of September.

Tether reported $1.5 billion in third-quarter operating profit as its excess reserves nearly doubled to $7.95 billion, according to figures released alongside its latest attestation prepared by independent accounting firm BDO.

The company held $191.5 billion in assets against $183.5 billion in liabilities at the end of September, leaving a reserve surplus of $7.95 billion, nearly double the $4.1 billion reported in June. Its assets included $132.4 billion in direct and indirect US Treasury bill holdings.

That exposure is comparable to South Korea’s $134.2 billion in US government debt and exceeds the United Arab Emirates’ $116.1 billion, according to August data from the US Treasury Department.

Tether also generated $4.5 billion in net operating profit during the first nine months of 2026, with income largely driven by US Treasury bills and reverse repurchase agreements, according to the company. Its Bitcoin reserves were valued at $8.37 billion, up from approximately $5.8 billion at the end of June.

Tether’s USDT remains the world’s largest stablecoin, accounting for around 60% of the $297.3 billion stablecoin market, according to DefiLlama data . On Friday, Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said in a post on X that USDT’s user base had surpassed 700 million, with adoption concentrated in emerging markets.

The stablecoin issuer has faced years of scrutiny over its reserve transparency. In August, the company announced the completion of its first full independent financial statement audit by KPMG US, although the audited statements were not made public.

Decrypt News Coins Binance Hack: Why Bitcoin Didn't Crash Like It Did in 2018

Binance lost about $6.4 billion, the largest crypto hack on record, yet Bitcoin fell about 3%, against nearly 11% in 2018 when the exchange was last attacked.

By Jose Antonio Lanz Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Bitcoin dipped to about $76,400 on Friday, roughly 6% below its post-Fed level, after Binance's record $6.4 billion hack, versus a fall from $10,740 to $9,690 in minutes in March 2018 over an attack that Binance said stole nothing.

Crypto's market value has grown from more than $400 billion in March 2018 to roughly $2.6 trillion, and U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs now hold roughly 1.3 million coins.

Binance says it has set aside more than $6.34 billion to cover losses, about $3 billion is frozen, and withdrawals should resume in 45 hours.

Bitcoin is down about 4% a day after the biggest crypto hack on record. In March 2018, a failed attack on the same exchange knocked nearly 11% off its price in minutes, and Binance said at the time that no funds had been stolen.

Binance has confirmed yesterday's attack, and Chainalysis and TRM Labs put the theft at roughly $6.4 billion , more than four times the previous record hack: the $1.5 billion Bybit heist of February 2025. Bitcoin dipped to about $76,400 on Friday, around 6% below where it traded after Wednesday’s Federal Reserve decision.

More than $1.3 billion in leveraged bets was liquidated, meaning trades placed with borrowed money that exchanges close automatically when prices move against them. And yet Bitcoin is holding relatively steady, all things considered.

The 2018 incident was a phishing and theft attempt : attackers took over accounts, created API keys (credentials that let trading bots act on an account) and used them to pump the obscure coin Viacoin while 31 accounts that had pre-deposited the coin sold it. Bitcoin fell from $10,740 to $9,690 within minutes and kept dropping to about $6,600 by April 5, though the market was already in a bear run after peaking near $20,000 in December 2017.

To have a grasp of the situation, the entire crypto market was worth just over $400 billion in March 2018 and is worth roughly $2.6 trillion now.

A big reason for that, and why panic doesn't hit markets the same way anymore, is U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs. Funds like BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust let people buy Bitcoin through an ordinary brokerage account, and they now hold roughly 1.3 million BTC, about 6% of the supply.

Their shareholders don’t keep coins on Binance, and sovereign wealth funds such as Mubadala and the Abu Dhabi Investment Council have been buying. BlackRock’s fund alone took in $136 million on Wednesday, per Farside Investors data.

These funds don’t tend to panic sell so easily, and those funds remain locked for long periods of time.

The theft began at 4:05 p.m. ET Thursday, after U.S. markets closed, so Thursday’s preliminary $17 million of ETF inflows predate it and Friday’s flow figures are the first real read on whether those holders are selling.

The attacker still holds more than 420,000 ETH and 18,270 BTC, about $2.4 billion that no stablecoin issuer can freeze. The amount doesn’t account for other tokens, which would increase the holdings to more than $3 billion.

TRM and Chainalysis tie the attack to the North Korean group behind Bybit, which after that heist converted about 84% of the stolen Ethereum into Bitcoin through Thorchain, a cross-chain swap network.

Binance says it has set aside more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover every loss, and it is buying the missing tokens on the open market and over the counter, meaning in private deals off the exchange. About $3 billion is frozen, deposits are operating normally, and withdrawals are on track to resume in 45 hours.

Market sentiment was already soft before the theft and slid further: CoinMarketCap’s Fear and Greed index, a 0-to-100 gauge of market mood, dropped to 36 points from 43 (now in “fear” territory after being “neutral” yesterday), and Bitcoin sits about 38% below its $126,080 record. Back in 2018, the market was well in “extreme fear” territory at 12 points on the scale when the incident happened. Traders were already in panic mode, and the attack just worsened an already ugly situation.

Glassnode data show long-term holders underwater on about 4 million coins bought between $85,000 and $118,000, and HashKey analyst Tim Sun said before the hack that the market’s problem “is not panic selling, but rather insufficient new buying interest.”

So, taken all together, what it all boils down to is this: A more optimistic market, much more liquidity, active long-term investors, a clearer regulatory framework, a sense of safety thanks to that regulatory clarity, quick action by stablecoin providers, and a price trend in recovery likely all played a role in keeping Bitcoin safe from a global panic despite the record-breaking hack.

Decrypt News Coins Binance Hack: Why Bitcoin Didn't Crash Like It Did in 2018

Binance lost about $6.4 billion, the largest crypto hack on record, yet Bitcoin fell about 3%, against nearly 11% in 2018 when the exchange was last attacked.

By Jose Antonio Lanz Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Bitcoin dipped to about $76,400 on Friday, roughly 6% below its post-Fed level, after Binance's record $6.4 billion hack, versus a fall from $10,740 to $9,690 in minutes in March 2018 over an attack that Binance said stole nothing.

Crypto's market value has grown from more than $400 billion in March 2018 to roughly $2.6 trillion, and U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs now hold roughly 1.3 million coins.

Binance says it has set aside more than $6.34 billion to cover losses, about $3 billion is frozen, and withdrawals should resume in 45 hours.

Bitcoin is down about 4% a day after the biggest crypto hack on record. In March 2018, a failed attack on the same exchange knocked nearly 11% off its price in minutes, and Binance said at the time that no funds had been stolen.

Binance has confirmed yesterday's attack, and Chainalysis and TRM Labs put the theft at roughly $6.4 billion , more than four times the previous record hack: the $1.5 billion Bybit heist of February 2025. Bitcoin dipped to about $76,400 on Friday, around 6% below where it traded after Wednesday’s Federal Reserve decision.

More than $1.3 billion in leveraged bets was liquidated, meaning trades placed with borrowed money that exchanges close automatically when prices move against them. And yet Bitcoin is holding relatively steady, all things considered.

The 2018 incident was a phishing and theft attempt : attackers took over accounts, created API keys (credentials that let trading bots act on an account) and used them to pump the obscure coin Viacoin while 31 accounts that had pre-deposited the coin sold it. Bitcoin fell from $10,740 to $9,690 within minutes and kept dropping to about $6,600 by April 5, though the market was already in a bear run after peaking near $20,000 in December 2017.

To have a grasp of the situation, the entire crypto market was worth just over $400 billion in March 2018 and is worth roughly $2.6 trillion now.

A big reason for that, and why panic doesn't hit markets the same way anymore, is U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs. Funds like BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust let people buy Bitcoin through an ordinary brokerage account, and they now hold roughly 1.3 million BTC, about 6% of the supply.

Their shareholders don’t keep coins on Binance, and sovereign wealth funds such as Mubadala and the Abu Dhabi Investment Council have been buying. BlackRock’s fund alone took in $136 million on Wednesday, per Farside Investors data.

These funds don’t tend to panic sell so easily, and those funds remain locked for long periods of time.

The theft began at 4:05 p.m. ET Thursday, after U.S. markets closed, so Thursday’s preliminary $17 million of ETF inflows predate it and Friday’s flow figures are the first real read on whether those holders are selling.

The attacker still holds more than 420,000 ETH and 18,270 BTC, about $2.4 billion that no stablecoin issuer can freeze. The amount doesn’t account for other tokens, which would increase the holdings to more than $3 billion.

TRM and Chainalysis tie the attack to the North Korean group behind Bybit, which after that heist converted about 84% of the stolen Ethereum into Bitcoin through Thorchain, a cross-chain swap network.

Binance says it has set aside more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover every loss, and it is buying the missing tokens on the open market and over the counter, meaning in private deals off the exchange. About $3 billion is frozen, deposits are operating normally, and withdrawals are on track to resume in 45 hours.

Market sentiment was already soft before the theft and slid further: CoinMarketCap’s Fear and Greed index, a 0-to-100 gauge of market mood, dropped to 36 points from 43 (now in “fear” territory after being “neutral” yesterday), and Bitcoin sits about 38% below its $126,080 record. Back in 2018, the market was well in “extreme fear” territory at 12 points on the scale when the incident happened. Traders were already in panic mode, and the attack just worsened an already ugly situation.

Glassnode data show long-term holders underwater on about 4 million coins bought between $85,000 and $118,000, and HashKey analyst Tim Sun said before the hack that the market’s problem “is not panic selling, but rather insufficient new buying interest.”

So, taken all together, what it all boils down to is this: A more optimistic market, much more liquidity, active long-term investors, a clearer regulatory framework, a sense of safety thanks to that regulatory clarity, quick action by stablecoin providers, and a price trend in recovery likely all played a role in keeping Bitcoin safe from a global panic despite the record-breaking hack.

Coinbase’s $719 million profit reveals a company caught between two crypto economies

Investment gains powered its rebound as prediction markets grew into a $200 million business, while record USDC holdings delivered shrinking revenue after rewards.

By Oluwapelumi Adejumo Senior Reporter • CryptoSlate

01 Coinbase reported a $719 million Q3 profit as its prediction-market business expanded and crypto investments increased. 02 The exchange added 643 BTC and 2,370 ETH, while prediction markets crossed $200 million in annualized revenue despite weaker spot trading. 03 Record USDC balances failed to prevent a 16.6% decline in revenue remaining after rewards, highlighting the cost of stablecoin growth. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Coinbase returned to a $719 million quarterly profit despite weaker crypto trading, buoyed by its investment gains in Bitcoin.

The exchange's third-quarter earnings , released Oct. 29, showed revenue of $1.216 billion, largely unchanged from the previous quarter but down 35% year over year. Crypto spot trading volume fell 8% to $134.5 billion, while transaction revenue declined 44% from a year earlier to $590 million.

Chief Financial Officer Alesia Haas said that Coinbase recorded its 15th consecutive quarter of positive adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, which reached $333 million, up 60% from the previous quarter.

Nevertheless, Coinbase reversed a $359 million second-quarter loss as its diversification strategy gained traction. Prediction markets surpassed $200 million in annualized revenue, while subscription and services contributed nearly half of net revenue.

The results also revealed growing costs associated with its USDC business and increased investments in Bitcoin and Ethereum.

Prediction markets emerge as Coinbase's fastest-growing business

Coinbase's prediction-market business has emerged as an increasingly important revenue source as sluggish cryptocurrency trading activity weighs on its traditional exchange operations.

According to its Q3 earnings presentation , prediction markets surpassed $200 million in annualized net revenue during the quarter, following an 82% compound quarterly growth rate since launch.

The company also reported a more than 60% increase in daily prediction-market traders compared with the previous quarter, making the product one of its fastest-growing businesses by revenue.

Coinbase's Prediction Market Annualized Revenue Exceeds $200 Million Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong described prediction markets as “one of the fastest-growing products in Coinbase history,” highlighting strong demand for cryptocurrency-related event contracts even during seasonally slower sports-betting periods.

The momentum is helping Coinbase diversify its transaction business beyond conventional spot trading.

Prediction markets and derivatives together accounted for approximately 25% of transaction revenue during the quarter, while customers trading event contracts also generated additional cryptocurrency spot trading activity.

These gains helped cushion declining crypto trading volumes. Coinbase's share of global crypto trading activity increased to 10.7% from 5.6% a year earlier, supported by growth across spot and derivatives products.

Meanwhile, subscription and services revenue increased 3% quarter over quarter to $570 million, representing 49% of net revenue.

Haas said the expansion was making Coinbase more resilient because prediction-market revenue was “less correlated to crypto volatility.”

The exchange plans to expand prediction-market engagement through additional event categories and product integrations while developing USDC-native clearing infrastructure to improve trading economics.

“We obtained CFTC approval for our own DCO to support predictions. And so what this means is we have the opportunity to own more of the stack. That means we can launch our own contracts, and we can also then earn better economics.”

Coinbase's record $22 billion USDC holdings conceal growing rewards costs

While prediction markets provided a new growth opportunity, Coinbase's established stablecoin business faced a different financial challenge.

The exchange reported a record $22 billion in average USDC balances across its products, a 49% year-over-year increase and about 30% of the stablecoin's average circulating supply.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

However, Coinbase's Q3 filing showed that stablecoin revenue declined 5.4% to $306.9 million from a reclassified $324.5 million a year earlier.

At the same time, USDC rewards expenses increased 15.8% to $129.2 million from $111.6 million, reflecting the growing cost of attracting and retaining stablecoin holders.

Subtracting the disclosed rewards expense from stablecoin revenue leaves approximately $177.7 million, down from $213 million in the comparable quarter.

That represents a $35.3 million decline, or 16.6%, despite the substantial expansion in USDC balances. The calculation excludes other income and expenses associated with the stablecoin business.

The divergence reflects competing pressures on Coinbase's commercial arrangement with Circle, the issuer of USDC.

Coinbase's filing attributed an $84.6 million positive revenue contribution to higher average USDC balances, while lower interest rates created a $52.8 million drag on revenue.

Interest income generated by the reserves backing USDC remains an important component of the economics shared between Coinbase and Circle. Lower rates therefore reduce the revenue available even as more customers hold the stablecoin.

The exchange has also been paying increasingly substantial rewards to support adoption. Still, the firm is looking to attract more participants to the USDC ecosystem. Haas said:

“Circle and we both have a goal to grow overall USDC market cap and adoption. In some cases, we could partner together to bring on more participants into the USDC ecosystem. We could also work independently to partner with various parties and bring them as partners on our respective platforms.”

Coinbase increases Bitcoin and Ethereum investments as crypto prices lift profits

Beyond its expanding trading and stablecoin operations, Coinbase also increased its direct exposure to cryptocurrency markets during the quarter.

A comparison of its second-quarter and third-quarter filings shows that the exchange's Bitcoin holdings for investment increased by 643 BTC, from 17,311 BTC at the end of June to 17,954 BTC in September.

Its Ethereum investment holdings also increased by 2,370 ETH, rising from 150,279 ETH to 152,649 ETH over the same period.

Together with other digital assets, the company's cryptocurrency investment portfolio increased in fair value from $1.47 billion to approximately $2.22 billion, a 51.5% quarterly increase.

Much of that increase reflected higher cryptocurrency valuations, which also contributed significantly to Coinbase's reported profitability.

The exchange recognized approximately $715 million in gains on crypto assets held for investment during the quarter, helping drive its $719 million net profit after three consecutive quarterly losses.

However, adjusted net income, which excludes those investment gains and certain other items, stood at $78 million.

The distinction highlights Coinbase's continued financial exposure to cryptocurrency prices even as prediction markets, stablecoins and subscription services become more prominent sources of revenue.

In its filing, Coinbase estimated that a hypothetical 50% increase or decrease in cryptocurrency prices would change the fair value of its investment portfolio by approximately $1.1 billion, with the resulting gain or loss flowing through its earnings.

Raymond and Isiah Garcia held a Minnesota family at gunpoint for more than nine hours, forcing the father to transfer over $8 million in crypto, in one of the clearest “wrench attack” prosecutions yet.

By Decrypt Agent Edited by Guillermo Jimenez

Judge's gavel. Source: Decrypt/Shutterstock

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Texas brothers Raymond and Isiah Garcia were sentenced to a combined 326 months for a September 2025 home-invasion robbery that forced a Minnesota man to hand over more than $8 million in crypto; both pleaded guilty in June.

The pair zip-tied the family and held them at gunpoint for over nine hours, even driving the victim to a cabin to retrieve hardware wallets, before fleeing and being arrested near Houston.

Chainalysis logged 46 violent incidents against crypto holders and $30 million-plus stolen in early 2026.

Two Texas brothers have been sentenced to a combined 326 months in prison for a violent home-invasion robbery in which they held a Minnesota family at gunpoint for hours and forced the father to hand over more than $8 million in cryptocurrency.

Raymond Christian Garcia and Isiah Angelo Garcia, both of Waller, Texas, were sentenced on Thursday to 180 months and 186 months respectively, or 15 and 15-and-a-half years, by U.S. District Judge Donovan Frank in St. Paul, according to the Justice Department. Both had pleaded guilty in June.

According to court documents, the brothers traveled from Texas to Grant, Minnesota, and on Sept. 19, 2025, broke into the victim’s home, zip-tied the family and held them at gunpoint for more than nine hours while demanding access to the father’s crypto accounts.

When he failed to transfer the amount they expected, they forced him to drive one of the brothers to the family’s cabin in upstate Minnesota to retrieve additional hardware wallets and move the funds. In total, they compelled him to transfer over $8 million. The pair fled after the victim’s son called 911, and were later arrested near Houston.

The case is a stark example of a “ wrench attack ,” in which criminals use physical force rather than hacking to seize crypto.
