Bitcoin fell after the Fed’s pause, but blaming interest rates misses the Binance shock

Investors were assessing the Fed's pause when a $6 billion Binance breach raised questions about access to their funds.

By Andjela Radmilac Senior Analyst • CryptoSlate

01 The Fed held rates at 3.75%–4%; both dissenters wanted a quarter-point increase. 02 Bitcoin fell below $77,000 as Binance reported a $6 billion security incident and liquidations surged. 03 Restrictive credit and suspended withdrawals affect leveraged traders through different channels. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

he Federal Reserve asked for more information before changing interest rates. Eighteen and a half hours later, the economy supplied it: growth was strong, inflation remained elevated, and households were spending more without buying much more. But before investors could settle what that combination meant for Bitcoin , a Binance security breach raised a more immediate concern about their ability to move money.

The Binance hack complicates any attempt to treat Friday's crypto selloff as a verdict on Wednesday's policy decision. Expensive borrowing and uncertainty over an exchange can both discourage risk-taking, but they work through different channels and demand different responses.

The Fed's 10–2 vote left its benchmark range at 3.75%–4%. Both dissenters, Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack, wanted a quarter-point increase. The disagreement concerned whether to raise borrowing costs immediately or wait for more evidence, leaving the prospect of another increase in December unresolved. An unchanged rate offered little basis to assume cheaper financing was coming.

Fed projections moved from a rate cut to another increase Selected FOMC meetings, October 2025–October 2026. Policy bars show the midpoint of the target range announced at each meeting. Projection bars show the median target midpoint for end-2026, calculated from published participant dots. Blank projection bars mean no new quarterly projections were issued, not a zero rate. Dates identify meetings, not forecast endpoints. Projections are individual policy assessments, not commitments or market odds.

Chart by CryptoSlate Source: Federal Reserve: target-rate history · Federal Reserve: 2025-12-10 projections · Federal Reserve: 2026-03-18 projections · Federal Reserve: 2026-06-17 projections · Federal Reserve: 2026-09-16 projections · Federal Reserve: October 29, 2025 decision · Federal Reserve: October 28, 2026 decision

Thursday's growth report also offered little reason for immediate relief. Gross domestic product expanded at a 3.4% annualized rate , up from 2.2% in the second quarter and slightly above the 3.2% economists expected in a Reuters survey. Annualizing expresses the quarter's growth as though that pace continued for a year; it does not mean output increased 3.4% in three months.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

Consumer spending and private fixed investment together grew at a 4.9% annualized pace. Because that measure excludes inventories, government spending, and trade, it suggested demand was robust beyond the components that can distort headline GDP.

The economy offered little evidence that it needed lower rates, while the inflation report supplied reasons to remain cautious about declaring progress secure. Yet the household data revealed the strain against which further tightening would have to be judged: an expanding economy could still leave consumers with less purchasing power.

The Fed's rate pause offered households little relief

Consumer outlays rose 0.5% in dollar terms , while the increase after inflation was less than 0.1%. Disposable income, measured after taxes and adjusted for inflation, fell 0.3%. Households collectively paid a larger bill for almost no increase in the goods and services they bought.

These figures explain how strong GDP can coexist with financial strain. Spending can support the economy even as prices absorb more of consumers' income, leaving them with less room to sustain purchases or absorb higher debt payments.

The inflation figures were similarly mixed. September's personal consumption expenditures price index was 3.6% above its year-earlier level: the core measure, excluding food and energy, rose 3.1%. Both annual readings matched Reuters' reported expectations , offering less basis for treating the release as a fresh inflation shock, even as price pressure remained uncomfortable for policymakers.

Over the third quarter, however, PCE inflation slowed to a 2.1% annualized pace, with core inflation at 2.5%, both below their second-quarter rates. Quarterly annualized changes and September's year-over-year comparisons cover different periods. Together, they showed progress alongside persistent price pressure, leaving policymakers to judge whether further tightening would secure that progress or place unnecessary pressure on households.

The immediate market response was also less decisive than the later decline suggested. Reuters reported that US stock-index futures pared existing losses after Thursday's releases. Remaining negative for the session while improving after the data is compatible with investors finding the news reassuring. By Friday morning, concerns about the returns on enormous AI investments were encouraging purchases of Treasuries, pushing yields and the dollar lower. Falling stocks therefore reflected a wider reassessment of risk, with several developments competing to explain the movement in prices.

Binance made access to money an immediate concern

The Binance breach added a problem that monetary policy could neither explain nor resolve. Interest rates influence the cost of financing a position, but an exchange's security and operating status influence whether customers can move the assets supporting it. Traders now have to assess both going into the weekend.

In its preliminary update , Binance estimated the incident's impact at approximately $6 billion and said roughly $3 billion had been frozen on-chain. The reimbursement promise addressed who would bear losses, but it didn't say when normal operations would resume or what the investigation might reveal. Nonetheless, customers don't have to expect an exchange to fail before deciding that uncertainty over access makes a leveraged position too uncomfortable to maintain.

Bitcoin keeps working throughout incidents like this while the businesses used to trade it experience disruption. Investors still rely on exchanges to hold collateral and execute transactions. Difficulty moving funds can therefore affect their willingness or ability to maintain positions, without any change to Bitcoin's underlying protocol.

By Friday morning, Bitcoin investors faced two unresolved risks: the future cost of financing and the reliability of the exchanges holding their assets. Restrictive rates could leave leveraged positions vulnerable before an exchange breach supplied another reason to reduce exposure. Separating those pressures would require examining trading around each announcement, although simultaneous releases and unrelated market developments would still limit any claim about causation.

Written by Christina Comben staff editor Edited by Andrew Fenton staff editor Written by Christina Comben staff editor Edited by Andrew Fenton staff editor

Will gold’s ‘infinite mint bug’ make Bitcoin more valuable?

Magazine Published Oct 30, 2026 A US fusion startup says it has turned mercury into gold. Could a potential increase in the gold supply strengthen Bitcoin’s claim to be a better form of digital gold?

They say all that glitters is not gold, and that took on a completely different meaning this month when a US fusion startup claimed it had produced gold from mercury.

Rather than chemical trickery, Marathon Fusion’s process relies on nuclear transmutation. Its research paper describes how high-energy neutrons from a deuterium-tritium fusion reaction can irradiate mercury-198, producing a radioactive isotope that decays into stable gold-197.

So, if gold has what some are calling an “infinite mint bug,” what will happen to the centuries-old metal so revered for its scarcity? And what, if anything, could that mean for Bitcoin as digital gold given it has a hard-capped supply?

Coinbase chief executive Brian Armstrong sees events playing out in Bitcoin’s favor, and compared the creation of “net-new gold with alchemy” to the lab-grown diamond industry. “But you can’t invent anything that will increase Bitcoin supply,” he said . “There will only ever be 21M.”

Perhaps inspired by the popularity of lab-grown diamonds, Marathon co-founder and chief executive Kyle Schiller tells Magazine he’s been fielding a lot of interest from jewelers.

“We have gotten a shocking amount of interest from people who want to do jewelry,” Schiller says. “As with regular gold, I think it’ll be mostly used as a store of value.”

But before gold bugs start quaking in their boots, Marathon’s achievement is still a long way from proving gold can be produced cheaply at scale.

Nikos Kavalis, managing director at precious metals research firm Metals Focus, tells Magazine, “We are nowhere near a stage where we can talk about production significance.”

The underlying nuclear process is scientifically plausible, but turning it into an economical industrial process is a whole new ball game.

Related: JPMorgan projects Bitcoin to outperform US stocks and gold over next decade

Marathon said it had produced stable gold at a rate 10 times CERN’s record, the European particle physics laboratory where scientists use powerful accelerators to study the fundamental building blocks of matter.

Nuclear fusion turned mercury into gold. Source: Marathon Fusion

But CERN’s ALICE experiment only produced an estimated 29 picograms of gold nuclei during its 2015-2018 run, and those nuclei only existed for fractions of a second before they were destroyed in collisions.

The company hasn’t publicly stated the exact quantity the experiment produced. Marathon research engineer Jake Harter tells Magazine the quantities remain extremely small, “right now still microscopic,” but the company hopes to reach “macroscopic milligram quantities in 2027.”

So the much larger numbers in Marathon’s paper are projections for a future fusion power plant, not based on output today.

The paper models production of about two tonnes of gold per gigawatt of thermal fusion power annually. To put that into context, the World Gold Council says that globally, mines produced 3,672 tonnes of gold in 2025, so a single future fusion plant’s output would be modest in comparison.

Even to reach those targets, Harter says the company would have to scale production of the enriched mercury used to produce gold, and of course it would need to build the fusion reactor itself.

“In the process of maturing this technology, we’ll also be working on studies demonstrating materials compatibility, mercury pumping and gold extraction,” he says.

It’s hard not to draw parallels like Armstrong’s between Marathon’s nuclear gold and lab-grown diamonds. Wholesale prices for lab-grown diamonds have fallen by more than 90% since 2018 as production has scaled up. Unlike older diamond substitutes like cubic zirconias, the composition of the newer lab grown diamonds is chemically identical to mined diamonds for a fraction of the price. Could the same thing happen to gold?

Marathon Fusion research paper. Source: Marathon Fusion

According to Nagham Hassan, a market analyst at investment platform eToro, the comparison with lab-grown diamonds is understandable, but “the economics are completely different.”

While diamond production became cheaper as factories scaled up, she said producing gold through nuclear fusion “would require highly complex infrastructure that does not yet exist commercially.”

Related: Bitcoin will become ‘less volatile’ and larger than gold: ‘The Bitcoin Standard’ author

Another complication is that the gold produced would be radioactive.

“The gold would need to be stored for a bit over a decade before dropping to banana-levels of [radio]activity,” Harter says, although, since most gold is “just stored as an investment,” he doesn’t see that as a major barrier to earlier commercialization.

A bigger problem is that it’s unclear whether the economics will ever stack up.

“There is no demonstration that the process is commercially viable,” Kavalis says. “There are theoretical revenue projections, but nothing about what it will cost to run the reactors.”

Bitcoin is often described as digital gold because its supply is limited by its protocol rules and capped at 21 million but Armstrong argues that no one can invent a way to fabricate future coins.

If a future technology like nuclear fusion could create another source of gold supply, that could in theory place downward pressure on the price.

“For any asset, a substantial increase in available supply would, other things being equal, put downward pressure on its market price,” Fabian Schär, professor of distributed ledger technology and fintech at the University of Basel, tells Magazine.

But with the first fusion reactors estimated to be at least a decade away, and plenty of questions remaining over the economic viability of this new form of alchemy, it’s unlikely to give Bitcoin prices a boost any time soon.

So for now, at least, Marathon’s work is more of a fascinating experiment with potentially interesting applications rather than an imminent threat to the gold market.

Peter Schiff and his buddies can breathe a sigh of relief.

posts.summary: Ripple closed out a highly busy Swell 2026 conference with major announcements and developments involving some industry and TradFi giants such as Coinbase, Robinhood, and BNY, as well as major regulatory news.
posts.summaryVi: Ripple closed out a highly busy Swell 2026 conference with major announcements and developments involving some industry and TradFi giants such as Coinbase, Robinhood, and BNY, as well as major regulatory news.
posts.content:
Ripple closed out a highly busy Swell 2026 conference with major announcements and developments involving some industry and TradFi giants such as Coinbase, Robinhood, and BNY, as well as major regulatory news.

Meanwhile, XRP Ledger developers proposed tighter control for permissioned assets. However, Ripple’s cross-border token has slumped to new local lows.

Perhaps the most notable takeaway for the XRP Army from Swell came directly from CEO Brad Garlinghouse, who pushed back against concerns that the company’s rapidly expanding RLUSD business has sidelined XRP. He described the latter as the firm’s “North Star,” saying Ripple only wants to pursue activities that benefit the cross-border token. Nevertheless, he acknowledged that RLUSD or fiat currencies can be more appropriate for certain financial transactions.

The stablecoin itself received several significant boosts that prompted the aforementioned claims within the Ripple community. Coinbase expanded access across several of its platforms, including Coinbase Prime, Coinbase Exchange, and its retail app, with support spanning XRPL, Ethereum, and Base.

Ripple also unveiled a broader partnership with Robinhood, under which RLUSD will play a role across Bitstamp, institutional settlement, and eventually the main application. Vlad Tenev’s company will integrate Ripple Treasury into its internal financial operations.

Separately, BNY expanded custody support to XRP and RLUSD, while Moody’s assigned the stablecoin an A2 long-term and P-1 short-term investment-grade rating, with the latter representing the agency’s highest short-term grade under its stablecoin framework.

Ripple said its product revenue run rate is approaching $900 million annually. The company also received final OCC approval to establish Ripple National Trust Bank, giving it a federally supervised entity designed to support RLUSD reserves and institutional digital-asset custody.

Ripple’s corporate-finance ambitions also grew, with Ripple Treasury bringing together AI-powered cash management, payments, forecasting, and liquidity tools, including 24/7 Returns for eligible businesses holding qualifying digital assets such as RLUSD.

The XRP Ledger is also receiving new institutional use cases as Ripple and C2FO are working to bring the latter’s Instant Pay settlement platform onto XRPL. They also want to use RLUSD to help suppliers receive funds in seconds rather than waiting days for conventional bank transfers to clear.

XRPL devs proposed four code changes designed to tighten restrictions around permissioned tokens, such as regulated stablecoins or tokenized funds that issuers only want approved accounts to hold. The proposed fixCleanup3_5_0 upgrade would close several remaining exceptions, including routes involving automated market makers, and would generally restrict unapproved holders to returning tokens to their issuer until authorization is granted.

At the same time, Flare joined the XRPL validator list, while the XRP Ledger Foundation dropped Anodos Finance since the project requested to be removed ahead of a planned validator shutdown by the end of the month.

Although Ripple had quite the impressive second part of October, the underlying token has fallen with the rest of the market. XRP was rejected at $1.40 on October 21 and the subsequent correction pushed it south to $1.25.

It rebounded in the following days and challenged $1.35 after the Fed paused interest rate hikes on Wednesday. However, the largest hack against any crypto exchange that unfolded earlier this morning resulted in a market-wide crash that drove XRP to a multi-month low of $1.19.

Despite recovering slightly since then, the asset remains 4% down on the day. It has slipped by 6% weekly, while its market cap has tanked to under $80 billion.

XRPL devs proposed four code changes designed to tighten restrictions around permissioned tokens, such as regulated stablecoins or tokenized funds that issuers only want approved accounts to hold. The proposed fixCleanup3_5_0 upgrade would close several remaining exceptions, including routes involving automated market makers, and would generally restrict unapproved holders to returning tokens to their issuer until authorization is granted.

At the same time, Flare joined the XRPL validator list, while the XRP Ledger Foundation dropped Anodos Finance since the project requested to be removed ahead of a planned validator shutdown by the end of the month.

Although Ripple had quite the impressive second part of October, the underlying token has fallen with the rest of the market. XRP was rejected at $1.40 on October 21 and the subsequent correction pushed it south to $1.25.

It rebounded in the following days and challenged $1.35 after the Fed paused interest rate hikes on Wednesday. However, the largest hack against any crypto exchange that unfolded earlier this morning resulted in a market-wide crash that drove XRP to a multi-month low of $1.19.

Despite recovering slightly since then, the asset remains 4% down on the day. It has slipped by 6% weekly, while its market cap has tanked to under $80 billion.

FBI and Secret Service join response to Binance’s $6.3B hack

Latest News Published Oct 30, 2026 US agencies are investigating the theft and helping trace stolen assets, while Binance says about $3 billion has been frozen.

Update (Oct. 30 at 9:04 pm UTC): This article has been updated to include FBI and US Secret Service statements reported by Reuters and Bloomberg, along with Binance’s latest recovery and withdrawal plans.

The US FBI and Secret Service have publicly acknowledged their involvement in the response to Binance’s $6.3 billion hack as efforts continue to trace and recover stolen cryptocurrency.

The FBI told Reuters Friday it was working with government and industry partners to assess the incident’s scope and potential impacts and coordinate investigative steps.

Secret Service investigators were also “working around the clock” with private-sector partners to recover stolen funds, a spokesperson told Bloomberg on Friday.

The cryptocurrency exchange revealed its cooperation with law enforcement in a Friday X post , without specifying the agencies involved.

The exchange has separately reserved more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses, including $5 billion already held in the affected cryptocurrencies. A spokesperson told Cointelegraph those tokens were in Binance’s custody , but declined to disclose wallet addresses, citing security concerns.

Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs attributed the attack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group.

Withdrawals remained suspended Friday. Binance said it aimed to begin reopening them in stages from Sunday, subject to security checks, with proof-of-reserves results also expected Monday.

Binance ranks as the largest cryptocurrency exchange by reserves with $134 billion in total assets. It had processed about $6 billion in outflows during the past 24 hours, according to DefiLlama .

In February 2022, the US Department of Justice said law enforcement agencies, including the FBI, helped seize 94,000 Bitcoin (BTC), valued at $3.6 billion at the time, which were linked to the 2016 Bitfinex exchange hack.

Decrypt News Law and Order Israel Extradites Alleged Nomad Bridge Exploiter to US Over $2.8M Theft: Report

Israel's Supreme Court ruled that exploiting a coding flaw can count as computer intrusion, even when the software allowed the transaction.

By Decrypt Agent Edited by Stephen Graves

Man in handcuffs. Source: Shutterstock/Decrypt

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Israel has extradited Alexander Block, formerly Alexander Gurevich, to the U.S. to face charges over the alleged theft of about $2.8 million from crypto bridge Nomad in 2022.

Prosecutors allege that his exploit exposed a flaw that other users then used to drain more than $186 million from a Nomad-controlled wallet.

Israel's Supreme Court rejected his appeal, ruling that exploiting a programming flaw can be unlawful computer intrusion even where the software permitted it.

Israel has extradited an Israeli-Russian citizen to the United States to face charges over the alleged theft of about $2.8 million from crypto bridge Nomad, Israel's State Attorney's Office announced on Thursday, according to a report in The Jerusalem Post .

Alexander Block, formerly known as Alexander Gurevich, was transferred to U.S. authorities early Thursday after unsuccessful appeals in Israel. He was arrested at Ben Gurion Airport in May 2025 while preparing to fly to Russia, shortly after changing his surname and obtaining a passport in his new name.

A federal grand jury in the Northern District of California indicted Block in August 2023 on four counts of computer fraud, one count of transporting stolen property and three counts of money laundering, according to Israel's Supreme Court judgment in the case. The U.S. requested his extradition in December 2024.

According to the U.S. extradition request, as set out in the judgment, a June 2022 software update left a flaw in Nomad's smart contracts that let users receive tokens on one blockchain without locking up the equivalent assets on another. Block, operating under the username "Bitlik," allegedly made six test transfers before carrying out four main transfers around August 1, 2022, receiving tokens worth more than $2.8 million. He then allegedly moved the tokens through several wallets and converted them into other cryptocurrencies to conceal their origin.

His actions exposed the flaw to other Nomad users, who drained a Nomad-controlled wallet holding more than $186 million in user funds, the request alleges. A few days later, Block returned some of the tokens and contacted a senior Nomad official on Telegram, offering to return the rest in exchange for payment for finding the flaw. He later cut off contact, and Nomad went to U.S. law enforcement.

The Jerusalem District Court approved Block's extradition in July 2025. On appeal, he argued that the transactions used functions available within Nomad's automated system, and that the public record of blockchain transfers undermined the money laundering allegations.

The Supreme Court rejected both arguments, holding that exploiting a programming flaw could constitute unlawful computer intrusion even where the software technically permitted the action, The Jerusalem Post reported. It also found that publicly visible transactions do not necessarily identify the people behind wallets or rule out efforts to conceal where funds came from.

Supreme Court President Isaac Amit later rejected Block's request for a further hearing, according to the State Attorney's Office.

The August 2022 exploit drained Nomad of nearly all its funds. Because it took little technical knowledge to copy the original attack, Paradigm researcher Sam Sun likened what followed to "a frenzied free-for-all," Decrypt reported at the time.

In December 2025, the Federal Trade Commission proposed a settlement with Illusory Systems, Nomad's operator, saying the bridge lost $186 million after hackers exploited a poorly tested software update. The settlement would require the company to return recovered funds to users who have not been reimbursed. Nomad recovered about $22 million in the days after the hack.

Decrypt News Law and Order Israel Extradites Alleged Nomad Bridge Exploiter to US Over $2.8M Theft: Report

Israel's Supreme Court ruled that exploiting a coding flaw can count as computer intrusion, even when the software allowed the transaction.

By Decrypt Agent Edited by Stephen Graves

Man in handcuffs. Source: Shutterstock/Decrypt

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

Israel has extradited Alexander Block, formerly Alexander Gurevich, to the U.S. to face charges over the alleged theft of about $2.8 million from crypto bridge Nomad in 2022.

Prosecutors allege that his exploit exposed a flaw that other users then used to drain more than $186 million from a Nomad-controlled wallet.

Israel's Supreme Court rejected his appeal, ruling that exploiting a programming flaw can be unlawful computer intrusion even where the software permitted it.

Israel has extradited an Israeli-Russian citizen to the United States to face charges over the alleged theft of about $2.8 million from crypto bridge Nomad, Israel's State Attorney's Office announced on Thursday, according to a report in The Jerusalem Post .

Alexander Block, formerly known as Alexander Gurevich, was transferred to U.S. authorities early Thursday after unsuccessful appeals in Israel. He was arrested at Ben Gurion Airport in May 2025 while preparing to fly to Russia, shortly after changing his surname and obtaining a passport in his new name.

A federal grand jury in the Northern District of California indicted Block in August 2023 on four counts of computer fraud, one count of transporting stolen property and three counts of money laundering, according to Israel's Supreme Court judgment in the case. The U.S. requested his extradition in December 2024.

According to the U.S. extradition request, as set out in the judgment, a June 2022 software update left a flaw in Nomad's smart contracts that let users receive tokens on one blockchain without locking up the equivalent assets on another. Block, operating under the username "Bitlik," allegedly made six test transfers before carrying out four main transfers around August 1, 2022, receiving tokens worth more than $2.8 million. He then allegedly moved the tokens through several wallets and converted them into other cryptocurrencies to conceal their origin.

His actions exposed the flaw to other Nomad users, who drained a Nomad-controlled wallet holding more than $186 million in user funds, the request alleges. A few days later, Block returned some of the tokens and contacted a senior Nomad official on Telegram, offering to return the rest in exchange for payment for finding the flaw. He later cut off contact, and Nomad went to U.S. law enforcement.

The Jerusalem District Court approved Block's extradition in July 2025. On appeal, he argued that the transactions used functions available within Nomad's automated system, and that the public record of blockchain transfers undermined the money laundering allegations.

The Supreme Court rejected both arguments, holding that exploiting a programming flaw could constitute unlawful computer intrusion even where the software technically permitted the action, The Jerusalem Post reported. It also found that publicly visible transactions do not necessarily identify the people behind wallets or rule out efforts to conceal where funds came from.

Supreme Court President Isaac Amit later rejected Block's request for a further hearing, according to the State Attorney's Office.

The August 2022 exploit drained Nomad of nearly all its funds. Because it took little technical knowledge to copy the original attack, Paradigm researcher Sam Sun likened what followed to "a frenzied free-for-all," Decrypt reported at the time.

In December 2025, the Federal Trade Commission proposed a settlement with Illusory Systems, Nomad's operator, saying the bridge lost $186 million after hackers exploited a poorly tested software update. The settlement would require the company to return recovered funds to users who have not been reimbursed. Nomad recovered about $22 million in the days after the hack.

A $10 sports bet helped trigger 13 felony charges against Kalshi in Utah

An undercover agent confirmed his Utah location before trading, giving prosecutors evidence to challenge Kalshi's claim to federal regulatory protection.

By Oluwapelumi Adejumo Senior Reporter • CryptoSlate

01 Kalshi and its founders face criminal prosecution in Utah after an undercover investigation uncovered 12 sports wagers totaling about $115. 02 The case escalates a national regulatory fight over whether federally supervised prediction markets must comply with state gambling laws. 03 A ruling favoring Utah could force Kalshi to restrict access to its contracts and expose its revenue to recovery claims in other states. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Utah filed 13 felony charges against Kalshi and named its two founders as co-defendants after an undercover agent placed $115 in sports bets.

The Oct. 28 criminal filing names KalshiEX, CEO Tarek Mansour and Chief Operating Officer Luana Lopes Lara, escalating a dispute over whether federally regulated prediction markets must comply with state gambling laws.

The prosecution follows an investigation in which a state agent placed 12 sports wagers totaling $114.87 on Kalshi between Sept. 13 and Sept. 26. The charges expose the company's founders to potential criminal penalties as federal regulators challenge Utah's authority to restrict the platform.

According to the filing, Special Agent Scott Eggerman created an undercover Kalshi account using a Utah residential address, phone number and locally issued debit card.

Before placing his first $10 wager on a Dallas Cowboys-New York Giants game, Kalshi allegedly required Eggerman to confirm his location through its location services.

Eggerman confirmed he was in Utah, but the platform permitted the transaction and collected a 44-cent fee.

He subsequently placed 11 additional wagers involving football, baseball, soccer and hockey events, generating further transaction fees for Kalshi.

Prosecutors cited those transactions in bringing 12 third-degree felony counts of online gambling promotion, one second-degree felony count of engaging in a pattern of unlawful activity and a misdemeanor gambling promotion charge.

The filing alleges that Kalshi collected revenue from unlawful gambling activity and reinvested the proceeds into its operations. It also cites public statements by Mansour and Lopes Lara describing their direct control over the company's management and business activities.

Both executives were named as co-defendants and issued court summonses rather than arrest warrants.

Kalshi rejected the allegations, describing the prosecution as a “crazy overreach” and accusing Utah of “playing politics.”

Kalshi faces criminal prosecution as CFTC challenges Utah's authority

The criminal case intensifies a jurisdictional fight that has already drawn intervention from the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC).

On Oct. 26, the CFTC and the US government sued Utah , seeking to prevent the state from enforcing gambling restrictions against federally regulated prediction markets.

The agency argues that the Commodity Exchange Act gives it exclusive jurisdiction over derivatives traded on registered exchanges, including Kalshi's event contracts .

Utah has maintained that federal registration does not exempt the platform from state gambling restrictions.

The state secured a significant legal victory in August when a federal judge rejected Kalshi's argument that federal law prevented Utah from enforcing its gambling laws. The Tenth Circuit subsequently declined to suspend enforcement while the company appeals.

Related Reading Kalshi must lock out state users after major court loss

Utah also filed a separate civil lawsuit on Oct. 20, seeking to prohibit Kalshi from offering contracts involving sports, elections, politics and other events to residents. The state wants Kalshi to implement court-approved geolocation controls and surrender profits generated from allegedly unlawful transactions.

The dispute gained further national backing on Oct. 29 when a coalition of 37 state attorneys general filed a brief supporting Utah's regulatory authority in the pending federal appeal.

The coalition's intervention increases pressure on Kalshi as it fights to preserve nationwide access to its contracts under a single federal regulatory framework.

A ruling allowing Utah to enforce its restrictions could force Kalshi to block affected contracts for residents and expose revenue earned in the state to recovery claims, while the company's founders confront a separate criminal proceeding.

posts.content:

Written by Helen Partz staff writer Edited by Yohan Yun staff editor Written by Helen Partz staff writer Edited by Yohan Yun staff editor

Binance says it holds $5B in matching tokens to cover hack losses

Latest News Published Oct 30, 2026 The exchange said it set aside more than $6.34 billion to cover losses and would include the assets in its next proof-of-reserves report.

Binance said Friday that it had set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses from its hack, with $5 billion already in held in the same tokens stolen.

“The $5 billion is held in the exact token assets that are required. These assets are in Binance custody,” a Binance spokesperson told Cointelegraph.

Binance did not disclose when it acquired the assets.

The spokesperson declined to disclose the wallet addresses, citing security reasons, but said that the holdings would appear in the exchange’s next proof-of-reserves report, which shows the assets it holds to back customer balances.

Binance said it provides weekly reports on its company funds to the Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA), the financial regulator of Abu Dhabi Global Market in the United Arab Emirates. The exchange said the requirement predated the hack.

The exchange has yet to confirm which tokens it still needs to purchase, when those purchases will be completed or how much stolen crypto has been recovered.

Related: EIP-7702 didn’t cause Binance hack, but may have amplified losses

The exchange confirmed Friday that it had suffered a $6.3 billion hack, the largest cryptocurrency theft on record . Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs said funds were drained from Binance wallets across 10 blockchains on Thursday and attributed the attack to North Korean hacking group TraderTraitor.

Binance said about $3 billion in affected assets had been frozen with help from blockchain partners. Those assets were excluded from the company funds set aside to cover losses.

CertiK told Cointelegraph that it needed more information from Binance to assess whether the claimed $5 billion in tokens matching those stolen could be independently verified on-chain.

Earlier Friday, CertiK CEO Ronghui Gu estimated that approximately $3 billion in frozen assets and Binance’s $1.17 billion emergency fund could cover about 66% of the reported losses, leaving a potential $2.1 billion gap.

Gu said the estimated gap represented about 1.3% of Binance’s reported $165 billion in exchange reserves. Those reserves include assets backing customer balances.

Blockchain analytics company Nansen told Cointelegraph that it could not verify what funds Binance had available beyond its roughly $1.16 billion emergency fund or where the money to cover the remaining losses would come from.

Binance founder Changpeng Zhao said Friday the company’s SpaceX holdings alone, linked to a $500 million investment in Elon Musk’s Twitter takeover, were worth more than $1 billion.

Binance co-founder Yi He said that the exchange’s revenue for the year was sufficient to cover the hack losses and that the company did not need to sell its stake in SpaceX.

Zhao also said Binance accumulates the cryptocurrencies it lists because customers can pay trading fees in those tokens. In a separate post, he said Gulf, Binance’s partner in Thailand, had offered financial support.

Zhao, who stepped down as CEO in 2023 and later served four months in a US prison over anti-money-laundering violations, remains a major Binance shareholder. Forbes estimated his personal fortune at approximately $115 billion.

Binance’s $6.3 Billion Hack Overshadows Hyperliquid’s Biggest Day

Someone stole about $6.4 billion from Binance. That is, by a wide margin, the biggest crypto theft that has ever happened, four times the $1.5 billion taken from Bybit in February 2025.

The money left across three different blockchains: roughly $3.5 billion in ETH, $1.4 billion in BTC, and $630 million on Tron (final accounting still underway).

Luckily, stablecoin issuers can freeze their own tokens; it’s a kill switch built into USDT and USDC. Tether and Circle used it, locking up about $2.39 billion between them. That’s 43% of the haul. That leaves somewhere between $2.6 and $3.2 billion still out there.

Aave also stepped in, freezing its V3 and V4 markets on Ethereum. That’s precautionary, given the worry is an attacker using stolen money to borrow against and leave the protocol holding bad debt.

As this was playing out, Binance stated it’s “aware of reports of a potential security issue” and that user funds are “completely safe,” and paused withdrawals on multiple networks. The clearest comment came from CZ, who no longer runs Binance but is its largest shareholder: it “does look like a hack,” and he expects user funds to be “fully covered.” Later in the evening, Binance announced that it has reserved over $6.34B in company funds to cover losses. So funds are indeed “safu.”

ZachXBT shared that the Binance hack funds were commingled with funds from the $388M Bitget exploit, leading him to believe it’s the same hacker group out of North Korea behind the attack. As for how it happened, Binance pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop which was compromised, allowing the attacks to submit the unauthorized transactions, before identifying "additional points of breach" in the following hours.

Markets did what you’d expect. Bitcoin fell below $797,000, ETH fell sub-$2,200 and BNB sub-$700. Over $1.33B in positions got liquidated on the day.

Unfortunately, this came after what was shaping up to be one of the most positive days for a crypto project in its history.

Earlier on Thursday, Trade.xyz announced that Intercontinental Exchange (the company that owns the New York Stock Exchange) is investing in it. The plan is a regulated U.S. venue offering round-the-clock perpetual futures built on Hyperliquid: stocks, indices, commodities, currencies and crypto, with its own exchange and clearing setup, pending CFTC approval.

Stanley Druckenmiller is joining as well, the first of a small group of outside market figures. He already owns the trade; his family office disclosed a $23 million position in Hyperliquid Strategies earlier this year.

So Hyperliquid has its path to a fully regulated perps offering inside the U.S., claims Stanley Druckenmiller as an investor ( and a tout on X ), and ICE’s CEO said that Hyperliquid was “bigger than NASDAQ.” Doesn’t get much better than that.

I am excited to be an investor in trade(xyz) as they partner with ICE to bring 24/7 perpetual futures on Hyperliquid to the United States. As a market participant, I am looking forward to to using their innovative product to enhance my investment process.

— Stan Druckenmiller (@standuquesne) October 29, 2026

HYPE shot as high as $97 on the day, up more than 20% at peak, before falling to $89 in the Binance hack aftermath. As of this morning, it’s at $93 and still up 8% on the day.

Unfortunately, now we have to deal with the Binance hack aftermath. Hyperliquid is a likely winner as a primary DEX option vs CEXs like Binance (which will likely be less trusted now.) But there’s also a good chance of the entire market being dragged down by fears of more exploits looming.

We will find out soon enough. Expect a bumpy ride…

Vụ hack trị giá 6,3 tỷ USD của Binance làm lu mờ ngày trọng đại nhất của siêu thanh khoản

Ai đó đã đánh cắp khoảng 6,4 tỷ USD từ Binance. Nói chung, đó là vụ trộm tiền điện tử lớn nhất từng xảy ra, gấp 4 lần số tiền 1,5 tỷ USD bị lấy đi từ Bybit vào tháng 2 năm 2025.Số tiền còn lại trên ba blockchain khác nhau: khoảng 3,5 tỷ đô la ETH, 1,4 tỷ đô la BTC và 630 triệu đô la trên Tron (kế toán cuối cùng vẫn đang được tiến hành).

May mắn thay, các nhà phát hành stablecoin có thể đóng băng token của riêng họ; đó là một kill switch được tích hợp trong USDT và USDC. Tether và Circle đã sử dụng nó, nắm giữ khoảng 2,39 tỷ USD. Đó là 43% của chuyến đi. Như vậy vẫn còn khoảng từ 2,6 đến 3,2 tỷ USD.

Aave cũng vào cuộc, đóng băng thị trường V3 và V4 trên Ethereum. Đó là biện pháp phòng ngừa, vì lo ngại kẻ tấn công sẽ sử dụng tiền bị đánh cắp để vay và khiến giao thức giữ nợ xấu.

Khi sự việc này diễn ra, Binance cho biết họ “đã biết về các báo cáo về vấn đề bảo mật tiềm ẩn” và tiền của người dùng “hoàn toàn an toàn” và đã tạm dừng rút tiền trên nhiều mạng. Nhận xét rõ ràng nhất đến từ CZ, người không còn điều hành Binance nhưng là cổ đông lớn nhất của nó: nó “trông giống như một vụ hack” và anh ấy hy vọng tiền của người dùng sẽ “được bảo đảm đầy đủ”. Vào buổi tối muộn, Binance thông báo rằng họ đã dành hơn 6,34 tỷ USD tiền quỹ của công ty để bù lỗ. Vì vậy, tiền thực sự là “an toàn”.

ZachXBT chia sẻ rằng số tiền hack Binance được trộn lẫn với số tiền từ vụ khai thác Bitget trị giá 388 triệu USD, khiến anh tin rằng chính nhóm hacker đến từ Triều Tiên đứng sau vụ tấn công. Về nguyên nhân sự việc xảy ra, Binance chỉ ra rằng máy tính xách tay của kỹ sư DevOps đã bị xâm nhập, cho phép kẻ tấn công gửi các giao dịch trái phép, trước khi xác định “các điểm vi phạm bổ sung” trong những giờ tiếp theo.

Thị trường đã làm những gì bạn mong đợi. Bitcoin giảm xuống dưới 797.000 USD, ETH giảm xuống dưới 2.200 USD và BNB xuống dưới 700 USD. Hơn 1,33 tỷ USD ở các vị thế đã được thanh lý trong ngày.

Thật không may, điều này xảy ra sau những ngày được coi là một trong những ngày tích cực nhất đối với một dự án tiền điện tử trong lịch sử của nó.

Trước đó vào thứ Năm, Trade.xyz đã thông báo rằng Intercontinental Exchange (công ty sở hữu Sở giao dịch chứng khoán New York) đang đầu tư vào đó. Kế hoạch này là một địa điểm được quản lý của Hoa Kỳ cung cấp các hợp đồng tương lai vĩnh viễn suốt ngày đêm được xây dựng trên Hyperliquid: cổ phiếu, chỉ số, hàng hóa, tiền tệ và tiền điện tử, với thiết lập trao đổi và thanh toán bù trừ riêng, đang chờ CFTC phê duyệt.

Stanley Druckenmiller cũng tham gia, là người đầu tiên trong nhóm nhỏ các nhân vật thị trường bên ngoài. Anh ta đã sở hữu giao dịch; văn phòng gia đình của ông đã tiết lộ một vị trí trị giá 23 triệu đô la trong Chiến lược siêu thanh khoản vào đầu năm nay.

Vì vậy, Hyperliquid có con đường dẫn đến việc cung cấp tội phạm được quản lý hoàn toàn ở Hoa Kỳ, Stanley Druckenmiller tuyên bố với tư cách là nhà đầu tư (và là người giới thiệu về X), và Giám đốc điều hành của ICE nói rằng Hyperliquid “lớn hơn NASDAQ”. Không tốt hơn thế nhiều.

Tôi rất vui được trở thành nhà đầu tư trong lĩnh vực thương mại (xyz) khi họ hợp tác với ICE để mang hợp đồng tương lai vĩnh viễn 24/7 trên Hyperliquid đến Hoa Kỳ. Với tư cách là người tham gia thị trường, tôi mong muốn được sử dụng sản phẩm sáng tạo của họ để nâng cao quá trình đầu tư của mình.

- Stan Druckenmiller (@standuquesne) Ngày 29 tháng 10 năm 2026

HYPE đã tăng cao tới 97 USD trong ngày, tăng hơn 20% vào thời điểm cao điểm, trước khi giảm xuống còn 89 USD sau vụ hack Binance. Tính đến sáng nay, nó ở mức 93 USD và vẫn tăng 8% trong ngày.Thật không may, bây giờ chúng ta phải giải quyết hậu quả của vụ hack Binance. Hyperliquid có khả năng chiến thắng với tư cách là tùy chọn DEX chính so với các CEX như Binance (hiện có thể sẽ ít được tin cậy hơn.) Nhưng cũng có khả năng cao là toàn bộ thị trường sẽ bị kéo xuống do lo ngại về nhiều vụ khai thác sắp xảy ra.

Chúng tôi sẽ tìm ra đủ sớm. Mong đợi một chuyến đi gập ghềnh…

Decrypt News Technology TRM and Chainalysis Tie $6.4B Binance Hack to North Korea's TraderTraitor

Both firms blame the group behind the Bybit hack, as Binance says it has set aside $6.34 billion of its own funds to cover user losses.

By Decrypt Agent Edited by Stephen Graves

North Korea and hacking. Image: Shutterstock/Decrypt

Add on Google Add Decrypt as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google.

TRM Labs and Chainalysis have both attributed the Binance hack to TraderTraitor, the North Korean group the FBI blamed for the $1.5 billion Bybit hack.

Chainalysis said it saw Binance funds commingling with proceeds of last month's Bitget exploit, which had been attributed to North Korean actors.

Binance said it has reserved more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover losses, $5 billion of it already held in the affected tokens.

Three blockchain analytics firms have attributed this week's hack of Binance to North Korea, with two of the largest naming TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking group, as responsible for what both describe as the largest crypto theft on record.

TRM Labs said it made the attribution "with high confidence," based on "robust on and off-chain intelligence." It put the theft at about $6.36 billion, moved out of Binance wallets on 10 blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes from 4:05 p.m. ET on Thursday. That is about four times the $1.5 billion Bybit hack of February 2025, which the FBI attributed to the same group, TRM noted.

Chainalysis , which put the total at about $6.4 billion, said the strongest evidence came when its investigators saw funds stolen from Binance commingling in real time with funds from last month's Bitget exploit , which had been attributed to North Korean actors.

A Chainalysis spokesperson told CNN the firm had "high confidence" North Korea was behind the hack. Singapore-based Pangolin Intelligence also told CNN it believed a North Korean hacking unit was responsible, based on "analyzing the on-chain activity related to this hack and correlating with information gathered from previous known incidents." North Korea has previously denied hacking allegations.

TRM and Chainalysis both said the attacker's operational wallet was funded through Tornado Cash, a crypto mixer. TRM said that and other features, including staging that began well before the theft, matched earlier North Korea-linked attacks such as the Bybit hack and April's KelpDAO exploit .

On Ethereum , the attacker used an EIP-7702 delegation, a feature introduced in Ethereum's Pectra upgrade that lets an ordinary wallet run smart contract code, to turn a Binance hot wallet into a sweeper it controlled, with 50 pre-signed authorizations prepared in advance, according to TRM. Binance wallets on the other nine chains sent funds to the attacker through ordinary signed transfers. In TRM's assessment, that points to a compromise of Binance's hot wallet signing infrastructure.

Binance has said its investigation began with a compromised engineer's laptop, but has since uncovered "additional points of breach." The Bybit attack also began with a single compromised machine: North Korean hackers planted malicious code in the infrastructure of wallet provider Safe after compromising a Safe developer's computer, Decrypt reported at the time.

The attacker has moved quickly to launder what it could not keep. Chainalysis said it is seeing "never-seen-before laundering patterns," with thousands of transactions in a short period suggesting the use of automation to circulate funds repeatedly among addresses. The attacker also sold USDT to market makers and borrowed ETH against USDT on lending protocol Aave to race issuers' freezes, according to TRM, and now holds more than 420,000 ETH and 18,270 BTC, about $2.4 billion beyond any issuer's reach.

Tether, Circle, Ripple and World Liberty Financial have frozen about $2.67 billion in stablecoins , and Arbitrum's Security Council froze 8,426 ETH and 74.6 million ARB, TRM said. Binance puts the total frozen at about $3 billion.

Binance has begun recovering affected assets for users and continues to work with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace, freeze and recover additional funds.

The company has already publicly committed to cover losses through… pic.twitter.com/UqtBd37Fpj

In an update on Friday, Binance said it has reserved more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover the incident, $5 billion of which is already held in the exact tokens that were stolen. It is buying the rest through market and over-the-counter channels, which "can take longer because some tokens may have low liquidity," the exchange said. Those figures do not include frozen assets.

"We will weather this storm," Binance said.

North Korean hackers have long targeted the exchange. In August 2025, Binance chief security officer Jimmy Su told Decrypt that North Korean attackers try to get hired at Binance every day, and called them the single biggest threat to crypto companies. On Wednesday, the U.S. Treasury sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity over North Korean IT worker schemes that moved millions of dollars in crypto.

Tin tức giải mã TRM và Chainalysis liên kết vụ hack Binance trị giá 6,4 tỷ USD với TraderTraitor của Triều Tiên

Cả hai công ty đều đổ lỗi cho nhóm đứng sau vụ hack Bybit, vì Binance cho biết họ đã dành 6,34 tỷ USD tiền riêng của mình để bù đắp tổn thất cho người dùng.

Bởi Decrypt Agent Biên tập bởi Stephen Graves

Bắc Triều Tiên và hack. Hình ảnh: Shutterstock/Giải mã

Thêm trên Google Thêm Decrypt làm nguồn ưa thích của bạn để xem thêm câu chuyện của chúng tôi trên Google.

TRM Labs và Chainalysis đều quy kết vụ hack Binance cho TraderTraitor, nhóm Triều Tiên mà FBI đổ lỗi cho vụ hack Bybit trị giá 1,5 tỷ USD.

Chainalysis cho biết họ thấy quỹ Binance có liên quan đến số tiền thu được từ hoạt động khai thác Bitget vào tháng trước, được cho là do các tác nhân Triều Tiên thực hiện.

Binance cho biết họ đã dành hơn 6,34 tỷ USD tiền của công ty để bù lỗ, 5 tỷ USD trong số đó đã được giữ trong các token bị ảnh hưởng.

Ba công ty phân tích blockchain đã quy kết vụ hack Binance tuần này là do Triều Tiên, trong đó có hai công ty lớn nhất có tên là TraderTraitor, một nhóm hack của Triều Tiên, chịu trách nhiệm về vụ mà cả hai đều mô tả là vụ trộm tiền điện tử lớn nhất được ghi nhận.TRM Labs cho biết họ đưa ra phân bổ “với độ tin cậy cao” dựa trên “thông tin mạnh mẽ trong và ngoài chuỗi”. Nó ước tính vụ trộm trị giá khoảng 6,36 tỷ USD, đã chuyển ra khỏi ví Binance trên 10 blockchain, hầu hết trong khoảng 20 phút kể từ 4:05 chiều. ET vào thứ năm. TRM lưu ý rằng con số này gấp khoảng bốn lần vụ hack Bybit trị giá 1,5 tỷ USD vào tháng 2 năm 2025 mà FBI quy cho cùng một nhóm.

Chainalysis, đưa tổng số tiền lên tới khoảng 6,4 tỷ USD, cho biết bằng chứng mạnh mẽ nhất được đưa ra khi các nhà điều tra của họ thấy số tiền bị đánh cắp từ Binance trộn lẫn với số tiền từ hoạt động khai thác Bitget vào tháng trước, được cho là do các tác nhân Triều Tiên thực hiện.

Người phát ngôn của Chainalysis nói với CNN rằng công ty "rất tin tưởng" Triều Tiên đứng sau vụ hack. Pangolin Intelligence có trụ sở tại Singapore cũng nói với CNN rằng họ tin rằng một đơn vị hack của Triều Tiên phải chịu trách nhiệm, dựa trên “phân tích hoạt động trên chuỗi liên quan đến vụ hack này và tương quan với thông tin thu thập được từ các sự cố đã biết trước đó”. Triều Tiên trước đây đã bác bỏ cáo buộc hack.

TRM và Chainalysis đều cho biết ví hoạt động của kẻ tấn công được tài trợ thông qua Tornado Cash, một công cụ trộn tiền điện tử. TRM cho biết điều đó và các tính năng khác, bao gồm cả việc dàn dựng đã bắt đầu từ lâu trước vụ trộm, khớp với các cuộc tấn công trước đó có liên quan đến Triều Tiên như vụ hack Bybit và khai thác KelpDAO của April.

Trên Ethereum, kẻ tấn công đã sử dụng ủy quyền EIP-7702, một tính năng được giới thiệu trong bản nâng cấp Pectra của Ethereum cho phép một ví thông thường chạy mã hợp đồng thông minh, để biến ví nóng Binance thành một trình quét mà nó kiểm soát, với 50 ủy quyền được ký trước được chuẩn bị trước, theo TRM. Ví Binance trên chín chuỗi còn lại đã gửi tiền cho kẻ tấn công thông qua chuyển khoản có chữ ký thông thường. Theo đánh giá của TRM, điều đó chỉ ra sự xâm phạm cơ sở hạ tầng ký ví nóng của Binance.

Binance cho biết cuộc điều tra của họ bắt đầu từ máy tính xách tay của một kỹ sư bị xâm nhập, nhưng sau đó đã phát hiện ra “các điểm vi phạm bổ sung”. Cuộc tấn công Bybit cũng bắt đầu với một máy bị xâm nhập duy nhất: Tin tặc Triều Tiên đã cài mã độc vào cơ sở hạ tầng của nhà cung cấp ví Safe sau khi xâm phạm máy tính của nhà phát triển Safe, Decrypt đưa tin vào thời điểm đó.

Kẻ tấn công đã nhanh chóng di chuyển để rửa những gì nó không thể giữ được. Chainalysis cho biết họ đang chứng kiến ​​“các mô hình rửa tiền chưa từng thấy trước đây”, với hàng nghìn giao dịch trong thời gian ngắn, cho thấy việc sử dụng tự động hóa để luân chuyển tiền nhiều lần giữa các địa chỉ. Theo TRM, kẻ tấn công cũng đã bán USDT cho các nhà tạo lập thị trường và vay ETH lấy USDT trên giao thức cho vay Aave để chạy đua với việc đóng băng các nhà phát hành, theo TRM, và hiện nắm giữ hơn 420.000 ETH và 18.270 BTC, vượt quá tầm 2,4 tỷ USD của bất kỳ nhà phát hành nào.

TRM cho biết Tether, Circle, Ripple và World Liberty Financial đã đóng băng khoảng 2,67 tỷ USD tiền ổn định và Hội đồng Bảo mật của Arbitrum đã đóng băng 8.426 ETH và 74,6 triệu ARB. Binance đưa ra tổng số tiền bị đóng băng vào khoảng 3 tỷ USD.

Binance đã bắt đầu khôi phục các tài sản bị ảnh hưởng cho người dùng và tiếp tục hợp tác với cơ quan thực thi pháp luật, tổ chức phát hành, công ty tình báo blockchain và các đối tác trong ngành để theo dõi, đóng băng và thu hồi thêm tiền.Công ty đã công khai cam kết bù lỗ thông qua… pic.twitter.com/UqtBd37Fpj

Trong bản cập nhật vào thứ Sáu, Binance cho biết họ đã dành hơn 6,34 tỷ USD tiền của công ty để trang trải vụ việc, 5 tỷ USD trong số đó đã được giữ dưới dạng chính xác các token đã bị đánh cắp. Sàn giao dịch cho biết họ đang mua phần còn lại thông qua các kênh thị trường và không cần kê đơn, việc này “có thể mất nhiều thời gian hơn vì một số token có thể có tính thanh khoản thấp”. Những con số đó không bao gồm tài sản bị phong tỏa.

“Chúng tôi sẽ vượt qua cơn bão này,” Binance nói.

Tin tặc Triều Tiên từ lâu đã nhắm mục tiêu vào sàn giao dịch này. Vào tháng 8 năm 2025, giám đốc an ninh của Binance, Jimmy Su, nói với Decrypt rằng những kẻ tấn công Triều Tiên cố gắng được thuê tại Binance mỗi ngày và gọi chúng là mối đe dọa lớn nhất đối với các công ty tiền điện tử. Hôm thứ Tư, Bộ Tài chính Hoa Kỳ đã xử phạt 10 cá nhân và một tổ chức liên quan đến các chương trình nhân viên CNTT của Triều Tiên đã chuyển hàng triệu đô la tiền điện tử.

Bắt đầu mỗi ngày với những tin tức hàng đầu ngay bây giờ, cùng với các tính năng độc đáo, podcast, video và hơn thế nữa.

Bitcoin mining difficulty hits 148 trillion as revenues fall to three-month lows

Bitcoin's network is approaching record computing power, but daily mining revenue near $33 per PH/s is leaving older machines underwater at higher electricity rates.

By Oluwapelumi Adejumo Senior Reporter • CryptoSlate

01 Bitcoin's mining difficulty surged 5.54% as miners added 185 EH/s of computing power, reversing a prolonged network decline despite the AI shift. 02 The 21% hashrate recovery has strengthened Bitcoin's network but intensified competition for block rewards, squeezing miners' earnings. 03 Some mining equipment can no longer cover electricity costs at 6 cents per kWh, exposing a widening divide between efficient and struggling operators. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Bitcoin's mining difficulty jumped 5.54% on Oct. 29 as recovering network computing power intensified competition among miners already facing shrinking revenues.

Data from Nodewitness shows the adjustment increased difficulty from 140.58 trillion to 148.36 trillion, following another 5.92% increase on Oct. 16.

The increase comes as Bitcoin miners rebuild the network's computing power despite an industrywide shift toward artificial intelligence infrastructure. However, the recovery is adding financial pressure, with mining revenue falling toward $33 per petahash per second daily, its lowest level since August.

Bitcoin miners rebuild network strength despite AI infrastructure shift

According to Real Vision chief crypto analyst Jamie Coutts, Bitcoin's mining network has staged a substantial recovery following one of its steepest contractions in years.

Coutts noted that the network's 14-day average hashrate declined 23% between its October 2025 peak and February 2026, marking the steepest decline since China's mining ban in 2021.

The contraction reflected several factors, including severe winter weather that temporarily disrupted operations and growing concerns that mining companies were abandoning Bitcoin production for more lucrative AI infrastructure opportunities.

Although the network initially recovered, its computing power weakened again through July, reinforcing concerns about the industry's long-term commitment to Bitcoin mining.

However, Coutts said that trend has reversed significantly since July 17.

According to his analysis, Bitcoin's hashrate has climbed 21% over the subsequent 102 days, adding approximately 185 exahashes per second (EH/s) and recovering to within 6% of its previous record.

He described the increase as the largest absolute amount of computing power added during a comparable hashrate recovery since 2018, although the percentage gain was less exceptional historically.

Data from Look Into Bitcoin also shows the network's computing power has reached its highest level in seven months, illustrating the scale of the recovery despite the industry's growing interest in AI infrastructure.

Chart Showing Bitcoin Network's Hashrate (Source: Look Into Bitcoin) The rebound is noteworthy because several publicly traded mining companies have increasingly shifted their business models toward high-performance computing and AI data centers, where long-term infrastructure contracts can provide more predictable revenue than Bitcoin mining.

Still, Bitcoin's network-wide recovery suggests that mining capacity is expanding elsewhere, potentially offsetting equipment being redirected or retired by companies pursuing AI opportunities.

The return of computing power also helps explain the latest difficulty increases.

Bitcoin automatically adjusts mining difficulty every 2,016 blocks, roughly two weeks, to maintain an average block production time of 10 minutes. When additional computing power causes miners to find blocks faster than expected, the network raises difficulty to restore that target.

For Coutts, the recovery signals strengthening network security and continued confidence among operators willing to deploy computing resources despite difficult market conditions.

He noted that additional computing power raises the cost of attacking the Bitcoin network, while miners' willingness to expand on thin margins suggests continued investment in its long-term prospects.

However, that growing competition carries a financial cost for the same companies securing the network.

Bitcoin mining revenue falls toward August lows

Bitcoin's rising difficulty means individual miners must expend more computational work to earn the same expected amount of BTC, putting additional pressure on operators already struggling with electricity and infrastructure expenses.

The latest 5.54% adjustment alone reduces expected Bitcoin earnings per unit of unchanged computing power by approximately 5.24%, assuming transaction fees and other conditions remain constant.

Across the two October adjustments, the reduction reaches approximately 10.5%.

That pressure is reflected in Bitcoin's hashprice, which measures expected daily mining revenue for each petahash per second of computing power.

Data from Startmining shows the metric has dropped to approximately $33 per PH/s per day, its weakest level since August. For comparison, Bitcoin's hashprice averaged $40 in September, when the network's difficulty was considerably lower.

This means miners are earning substantially less revenue from the same computing capacity, even before accounting for electricity, maintenance, hosting and financing costs.

The impact is particularly severe for operators using older, less efficient mining equipment.

For example, at a gross hashprice of $33.35, equipment operating at 25 joules per terahash would generate approximately $32.68 daily per PH/s after an assumed 2% mining pool fee.

At an electricity tariff of 6 cents per kilowatt-hour, however, the same equipment would incur a daily power bill of $36, producing a $3.32 shortfall before other operating expenses.

More efficient equipment rated at 20 J/TH would spend $28.80 on electricity under identical conditions, leaving a modest surplus before additional costs.

This illustrates how the network's recovery is widening the financial divide between miners with access to cheap electricity and efficient machines and those operating older equipment at higher costs.

For miners operating at 25 J/TH, the current hashprice means electricity must cost approximately 5.45 cents per kilowatt-hour or less just to cover the power consumed by their machines.

The economics create a growing challenge for miners seeking to expand their computing capacity.

Additional mining equipment strengthens Bitcoin's network, but it also raises competition for the available block rewards, putting further pressure on the revenue that supports those investments.

Độ khó khai thác bitcoin đạt 148 nghìn tỷ khi doanh thu giảm xuống mức thấp nhất trong ba tháng

Mạng Bitcoin đang đạt đến sức mạnh tính toán kỷ lục, nhưng doanh thu khai thác hàng ngày gần 33 USD/PH/s đang khiến các máy cũ phải hoạt động ở mức giá điện cao hơn.

Bởi Oluwapelumi Adejumo Phóng viên cao cấp • CryptoSlate

Vào ngày 01 tháng 1, độ khó khai thác của Bitcoin đã tăng 5,54% khi các công ty khai thác bổ sung thêm 185 EH/s sức mạnh tính toán, đảo ngược tình trạng suy giảm mạng kéo dài bất chấp sự thay đổi của AI. 02 Tỷ lệ phục hồi hashrate 21% đã củng cố mạng lưới Bitcoin nhưng làm tăng thêm sự cạnh tranh về phần thưởng khối, làm giảm thu nhập của người khai thác. 03 Một số thiết bị khai thác không còn có thể trang trải chi phí điện ở mức 6 xu mỗi kWh, làm lộ ra khoảng cách ngày càng lớn giữa các nhà khai thác hiệu quả và đang gặp khó khăn. Đặt CryptoSlate được ưu tiên trên Chia sẻ

Độ khó khai thác của Bitcoin đã tăng 5,54% vào ngày 29 tháng 10 khi sức mạnh tính toán mạng phục hồi làm tăng thêm sự cạnh tranh giữa các thợ đào vốn đang phải đối mặt với doanh thu bị thu hẹp.

Dữ liệu từ Nodewitness cho thấy việc điều chỉnh tăng độ khó từ 140,58 nghìn tỷ lên 148,36 nghìn tỷ, sau mức tăng 5,92% khác vào ngày 16 tháng 10.

Sự gia tăng này xảy ra khi các công ty khai thác Bitcoin xây dựng lại sức mạnh tính toán của mạng bất chấp sự thay đổi toàn ngành sang cơ sở hạ tầng trí tuệ nhân tạo. Tuy nhiên, sự phục hồi đang gây thêm áp lực tài chính, với doanh thu khai thác giảm xuống còn 33 USD mỗi petahash mỗi giây, mức thấp nhất kể từ tháng 8.

Các công ty khai thác bitcoin xây dựng lại sức mạnh mạng bất chấp sự thay đổi cơ sở hạ tầng AI

Theo nhà phân tích tiền điện tử trưởng của Real Vision, Jamie Coutts, mạng khai thác Bitcoin đã có sự phục hồi đáng kể sau một trong những đợt suy thoái mạnh nhất trong nhiều năm.

Coutts lưu ý rằng hashrate trung bình trong 14 ngày của mạng đã giảm 23% từ mức đỉnh tháng 10 năm 2025 đến tháng 2 năm 2026, đánh dấu mức giảm mạnh nhất kể từ lệnh cấm khai thác của Trung Quốc vào năm 2021.

Sự co lại phản ánh một số yếu tố, bao gồm thời tiết mùa đông khắc nghiệt khiến hoạt động tạm thời bị gián đoạn và mối lo ngại ngày càng tăng rằng các công ty khai thác đang từ bỏ việc sản xuất Bitcoin để có cơ hội cơ sở hạ tầng AI sinh lợi hơn.

Mặc dù mạng ban đầu đã phục hồi nhưng sức mạnh tính toán của nó lại suy yếu cho đến tháng 7, củng cố mối lo ngại về cam kết lâu dài của ngành đối với việc khai thác Bitcoin.

Tuy nhiên, Coutts cho rằng xu hướng đó đã đảo chiều đáng kể kể từ ngày 17/7.

Theo phân tích của ông, hashrate của Bitcoin đã tăng 21% trong 102 ngày tiếp theo, thêm khoảng 185 exahash mỗi giây (EH/s) và phục hồi trong vòng 6% so với kỷ lục trước đó.

Ông mô tả mức tăng này là lượng sức mạnh tính toán tuyệt đối lớn nhất được thêm vào trong quá trình phục hồi hashrate tương đương kể từ năm 2018, mặc dù mức tăng phần trăm ít đặc biệt hơn trong lịch sử.

Dữ liệu từ Look Into Bitcoin cũng cho thấy sức mạnh tính toán của mạng đã đạt mức cao nhất trong 7 tháng, minh họa quy mô phục hồi bất chấp mối quan tâm ngày càng tăng của ngành đối với cơ sở hạ tầng AI.Biểu đồ hiển thị tốc độ băm của mạng Bitcoin (Nguồn: Look Into Bitcoin) Sự phục hồi này rất đáng chú ý vì một số công ty khai thác được giao dịch công khai đã ngày càng chuyển mô hình kinh doanh của họ sang các trung tâm dữ liệu AI và điện toán hiệu suất cao, nơi các hợp đồng cơ sở hạ tầng dài hạn có thể mang lại doanh thu dễ dự đoán hơn so với khai thác Bitcoin.

Tuy nhiên, sự phục hồi trên toàn mạng của Bitcoin cho thấy năng lực khai thác đang mở rộng ở những nơi khác, có khả năng bù đắp cho việc thiết bị đang được chuyển hướng hoặc ngừng hoạt động bởi các công ty theo đuổi cơ hội AI.

Sự trở lại của sức mạnh tính toán cũng giúp giải thích sự gia tăng độ khó mới nhất.

Bitcoin tự động điều chỉnh độ khó khai thác sau mỗi 2.016 khối, khoảng hai tuần, để duy trì thời gian sản xuất khối trung bình là 10 phút. Khi sức mạnh tính toán bổ sung khiến thợ mỏ tìm thấy khối nhanh hơn dự kiến, mạng sẽ gặp khó khăn hơn trong việc khôi phục mục tiêu đó.

Bắt đầu với những câu chuyện quan trọng. Biết bối cảnh đằng sau các tiêu đề và cái nhìn rõ ràng về nội dung sẽ xem tiếp theo.

Đọc liên quan Sự gia tăng độ khó tiếp theo của Bitcoin có thể khiến một số giàn khoan kiếm được ít hơn hóa đơn tiền điện của họ

Đối với Coutts, sự phục hồi báo hiệu việc củng cố an ninh mạng và tiếp tục tạo niềm tin cho các nhà khai thác sẵn sàng triển khai tài nguyên máy tính bất chấp điều kiện thị trường khó khăn.

Ông lưu ý rằng sức mạnh tính toán bổ sung sẽ làm tăng chi phí tấn công mạng Bitcoin, trong khi việc các thợ mỏ sẵn sàng mở rộng với tỷ suất lợi nhuận thấp cho thấy việc tiếp tục đầu tư vào triển vọng dài hạn của nó.

Tuy nhiên, sự cạnh tranh ngày càng tăng đó mang lại chi phí tài chính cho chính các công ty bảo vệ mạng.

Doanh thu khai thác bitcoin giảm xuống mức thấp nhất trong tháng 8

Độ khó ngày càng tăng của Bitcoin có nghĩa là các thợ đào riêng lẻ phải thực hiện nhiều công việc tính toán hơn để kiếm được cùng số lượng BTC dự kiến, gây thêm áp lực cho các nhà khai thác vốn đang phải vật lộn với chi phí điện và cơ sở hạ tầng.

Chỉ riêng lần điều chỉnh 5,54% mới nhất đã làm giảm thu nhập Bitcoin dự kiến ​​trên mỗi đơn vị sức mạnh tính toán không thay đổi khoảng 5,24%, giả sử phí giao dịch và các điều kiện khác không đổi.

Qua hai lần điều chỉnh tháng 10, mức giảm đạt xấp xỉ 10,5%.

Áp lực đó được phản ánh qua hashprice của Bitcoin, thước đo doanh thu khai thác hàng ngày dự kiến ​​cho mỗi petahash trên giây sức mạnh tính toán.

Dữ liệu từ Startmining cho thấy số liệu này đã giảm xuống khoảng 33 USD mỗi PH/s mỗi ngày, mức thấp nhất kể từ tháng 8. Để so sánh, giá băm của Bitcoin trung bình là 40 USD vào tháng 9, khi độ khó của mạng thấp hơn đáng kể.

Điều này có nghĩa là các thợ đào đang kiếm được doanh thu ít hơn đáng kể từ cùng một khả năng tính toán, ngay cả trước khi tính chi phí điện, bảo trì, lưu trữ và tài chính.

Tác động đặc biệt nghiêm trọng đối với những người vận hành sử dụng thiết bị khai thác cũ, kém hiệu quả hơn.Ví dụ: với tổng giá băm là 33,35 USD, thiết bị hoạt động ở tốc độ 25 joules mỗi terahash sẽ tạo ra khoảng 32,68 USD mỗi ngày cho mỗi PH/s sau khi tính phí nhóm khai thác giả định là 2%.

Tuy nhiên, với mức giá điện là 6 cent/kWh, thiết bị tương tự sẽ phải chịu hóa đơn tiền điện hàng ngày là 36 USD, tạo ra mức thiếu hụt 3,32 USD trước các chi phí vận hành khác.

Thiết bị hiệu quả hơn được đánh giá ở mức 20 J/TH sẽ chi 28,80 USD tiền điện trong các điều kiện giống nhau, để lại mức thặng dư khiêm tốn trước khi có thêm chi phí.

Điều này minh họa sự phục hồi của mạng đang mở rộng khoảng cách tài chính giữa những người khai thác có khả năng tiếp cận với điện giá rẻ và máy móc hiệu quả và những người vận hành thiết bị cũ với chi phí cao hơn.

Đối với các máy khai thác hoạt động ở tốc độ 25 J/TH, giá băm hiện tại có nghĩa là điện phải có giá khoảng 5,45 cent mỗi kilowatt giờ hoặc ít hơn chỉ để trang trải lượng điện năng tiêu thụ cho máy của họ.

Nền kinh tế tạo ra thách thức ngày càng tăng đối với các thợ mỏ đang tìm cách mở rộng khả năng tính toán của họ.

Thiết bị khai thác bổ sung củng cố mạng lưới Bitcoin, nhưng nó cũng làm tăng sự cạnh tranh về phần thưởng khối có sẵn, gây thêm áp lực lên doanh thu hỗ trợ các khoản đầu tư đó.
