Tháng Mười Đen của An ninh mạng: Cách tự bảo vệ mình

Tạp chí Xuất bản ngày 28 tháng 10 năm 2026 Mỗi ngày đều có tin tức về một cuộc tấn công khác do AI cung cấp hoặc một lỗ hổng mới được phát hiện. Đây là những gì đang xảy ra và cách những người bình thường có thể tự bảo vệ mình trực tuyến.

Các chuyên gia an ninh mạng đang có một tháng tàn khốc.

Cái được mệnh danh là Tháng Mười Đen vẫn chưa kết thúc và nó đã gây ra hàng chục cuộc tấn công mạng lớn và các lỗ hổng do AI xác định trên internet.

Khi các lỗ hổng nghiêm trọng trong PHP, ngôn ngữ lập trình được khoảng 70% trang web sử dụng, được phát hiện nhờ sự trợ giúp của các công cụ AI và được PHP Foundation tiết lộ vào ngày 21 tháng 10, cuộc đua vá lỗi máy chủ trên toàn thế giới đã bắt đầu.

Nhà cung cấp dịch vụ đám mây Cloudflare đã báo cáo hàng triệu nỗ lực khai thác lỗ hổng sau khi được tiết lộ, sau hàng nghìn nỗ lực trong những giờ trước đó.

Một số quốc gia, bao gồm Pháp và Phần Lan, đã tạm thời rút quyền truy cập vào một số trang web nhất định trong khi Cơ quan An ninh Quốc gia Hoa Kỳ (NSA) cảnh báo các tổ chức phải vá lỗ hổng ngay lập tức hoặc đưa các hệ thống bị ảnh hưởng vào trạng thái ngoại tuyến.

Illia Polosukhin, người sáng lập NEAR cho biết: “Hiện chúng tôi đang ở Security Armageddon. Cố vấn an ninh trưởng của Anthropic, Jason Clinton, cảnh báo rằng, “mọi thứ đã trở nên tồi tệ như thế nào trong 4 ngày qua, chúng sẽ trở nên tồi tệ hơn rất nhiều trước khi trở nên tốt hơn”.

Công dân Vương quốc Anh thậm chí còn được khuyến khích “sẵn sàng” cho trường hợp khẩn cấp, chẳng hạn như thời tiết khắc nghiệt hoặc các cuộc tấn công mạng, có thể cắt đứt quyền truy cập vào cơ sở hạ tầng quan trọng như nước, điện hoặc internet. Cơ sở quân sự của Hoa Kỳ đã được yêu cầu chuẩn bị cho 90 ngày hoạt động độc lập theo sáng kiến ​​FORTRESS.

Ngoài việc đổ xô đi dự trữ thực phẩm đóng hộp và máy bộ đàm, người dân bình thường còn có thể làm gì khác để giảm thiểu mức độ phơi nhiễm?

"Nó thực sự tồi tệ. Có vẻ như phần còn lại của Internet đang thức tỉnh trước thực tế mà chúng ta đã có ba tháng trước", Rob Hamilton, một nhà nghiên cứu bảo mật Bitcoin tham gia vào Nhóm Bitcoin Red, nói với Magazine.

Chính phủ Anh đang kêu gọi người dân sẵn sàng cho trường hợp khẩn cấp. Nguồn: gov.uk

Trong khoảng một tuần qua, nền tảng đám mây Rail đã tiết lộ rằng kẻ tấn công đã truy cập và giải mã thông tin đăng nhập của khách hàng cũng như khóa API, dường như nhắm mục tiêu vào các nhà cung cấp AI.

Liên quan: Pháp là nơi nguy hiểm nhất thế giới đối với người chơi Bitcoin: 90 cuộc tấn công trong 7 tháng

Công ty xét nghiệm y tế khổng lồ Quest Diagnostics xác nhận có sự vi phạm dữ liệu sức khỏe bệnh nhân tư nhân, trong khi công ty bảo mật Ấn Độ eMudhra bị phát hiện có 8 cơ quan cấp chứng chỉ kỹ thuật số có khóa yếu có khả năng cho phép kẻ tấn công mạo danh các trang web đáng tin cậy. Và nền tảng lưu trữ mã GitHub đã trải qua một sự gián đoạn dịch vụ lớn, điều này làm nổi bật mức độ phụ thuộc của thế giới phần mềm vào cơ sở hạ tầng dùng chung.Giám đốc bảo mật cấp cao của GitHub, Austin Devers, cho biết những sự cố như thế này là một “lời nhắc nhở rõ ràng rằng độ tin cậy đòi hỏi phải làm việc liên tục”, bởi vì sự phát triển hiện đại “rất kết nối”.

Sự cố an ninh đường sắt. Nguồn: Đường sắt

Jonathan Riss, nhà phân tích tình báo OSINT và blockchain tại công ty bảo mật blockchain CertiK, nói với Magazine:

Thật không may, ông nói thêm rằng khả năng tìm ra lỗ hổng của AI không tương xứng với khả năng sửa chúng:

Một lý do khiến vấn đề ngày càng trở nên tồi tệ hơn là do AI đã thay đổi tính kinh tế của an ninh mạng.

Những gì từng đòi hỏi nguồn lực quốc gia và các tin tặc tinh vi để thực hiện giờ đây có thể đạt được bởi một thiếu niên ở tầng hầm ở đâu đó.

Doanh nhân và nhà đầu tư AI Matt Shumer nói rằng AI cho phép người dùng không có kỹ thuật tìm ra điểm yếu và khai thác chúng, khiến những người bảo vệ phải “đua nhau để theo kịp”.

Devers cho biết các công cụ bảo mật được hỗ trợ bởi AI đang hạ thấp “đáng kể” rào cản đối với việc “phát hiện các lỗ hổng phức tạp, sâu xa trong các cơ sở mã được sử dụng rộng rãi”.

Liên quan: Keystone cho biết vi phạm trang web đã làm lộ địa chỉ của người mua ví phần cứng

Có một số bước thực tế mà người dân bình thường có thể sử dụng để giữ an toàn trực tuyến hơn trong giai đoạn đầy biến động này.

Internet đang bị tấn công. Nguồn: Matt Shumer

Shumer khuyên bạn nên tránh xa các trang web mà bạn không biết và chắc chắn không nhập mật khẩu hoặc số thẻ vào các trang web không quen thuộc “cho đến khi điều này kết thúc” vì các trang web nhỏ hơn “ít có khả năng được vá lỗi nhất”.

Xóa mọi ứng dụng bạn không sử dụng và rút phích cắm các tiện ích thông minh mà bạn không cần. Giữ một ít tiền mặt ở nhà và đủ đồ tạp hóa trong vài ngày, “nếu bạn muốn cẩn thận hơn”.

Devers cho biết cách phòng thủ tốt nhất là “khóa các điểm truy cập cá nhân và giữ cho dấu chân tổng thể ở mức nhỏ”. Bật Xác thực đa yếu tố (MFA) trên tất cả các tài khoản, lý tưởng nhất là sử dụng ứng dụng xác thực hoặc khóa bảo mật phần cứng thay vì tin nhắn văn bản.

Ông nói: Không bao giờ sử dụng lại mật khẩu. “Tạo mật khẩu mạnh, duy nhất cho mọi trang web và định kỳ ngắt kết nối các quyền của ứng dụng cũ hoặc kết nối của bên thứ ba mà bạn không còn sử dụng nữa”. Luôn cập nhật thiết bị và trình duyệt web của bạn một cách tự động:

Trong khi sự gia tăng đáng báo động về các sự cố bảo mật đã khiến một số người nắm giữ tiền điện tử phải xem xét các lựa chọn thay thế và một số chuyên gia đưa ra lời khuyên không nên tự quản lý, thì những người khác, chẳng hạn như người ủng hộ Bitcoin và giám đốc an ninh của Casa, Jameson Lopp, lại nhắc nhở người dùng rằng điều đó đã làm thất bại toàn bộ mục đích.

Riss khuyên bạn nên tách số tiền nhỏ mà bạn dự định sử dụng vào ví nóng, khỏi khoản nắm giữ dài hạn trong ví phần cứng và để “thực sự đọc những gì bạn đang ký thay vì phê duyệt một cách mù quáng”.

Mặc dù các biện pháp phòng ngừa này có thể làm giảm khả năng bị tấn công của bạn, nhưng người dùng hàng ngày chỉ có thể khóa các sự cố cục bộ và có rất ít khả năng ảnh hưởng đến các vấn đề rộng hơn.

Ông nói, bạn có thể “giảm bán kính vụ nổ mà không ngăn chặn được sự xâm phạm cơ sở hạ tầng”.

Vì vậy, mặc dù người dùng có thể cải thiện vệ sinh mạng của mình nhưng cuối cùng, “gánh nặng về cấu trúc lại thuộc về các nền tảng và nhà cung cấp”.

posts.title: DTCC unit launches tokenization services
posts.titleVi: Đơn vị DTCC ra mắt dịch vụ token hóa
posts.content:
1.60% TRX $0.3297 0.55% LINK $11.80 2.48% ZEC $1,309.20 0.27% ADA $0.2058 0.29% XRP $1.32 0.28% ETH $2,358.36 0.39% BTC $81,249.25 0.44% XMR $599.07 0.86% BNB $756.84 1.52% XLM $0.1729 1.68% SOL $102.45 1.17% HYPE $81.03 0.39%

Written by Zoltan Vardai staff writer Edited by Robert Lakin staff editor Written by Zoltan Vardai staff writer Edited by Robert Lakin staff editor

Latest News Published Oct 28, 2026 The post-trade market infrastructure provider said the tokenization services will create a “practical path” for tokenized securities adoption.

The Depository Trust Company (DTC), a subsidiary of The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), has launched tokenization services enabling eligible users to mint tokenized representations of securities held at DTC.

DTCC clients are eligible to use the DTCC Tokenization Service (DTS). DTS will convert between traditional and tokenized forms of securities that are transferable to digital wallets and retain the same ownership rights and investor protections as their traditional counterparts, the company announced on Wednesday.

The post-trade market infrastructure provider said that 20 of its clients have signed agreements to access the services, including Alpaca, Citadel Securities, Citi, Clear Street, DriveWealth, Fidelity Investments, Interchange Clearing and JPMorgan.

DTC has more than $114 trillion in assets under custody, including stocks and exchange-traded funds. The company said its service will create a “practical path” for tokenized securities adoption.

In December 2025, the US Securities and Exchange Commission issued a “no action” letter stating that it would not recommend enforcement action against DTCC’s subsidiary in relation to its proposed tokenization program.

In May, DTCC said it planned a full service launch of trading of tokenized securities in October 2026, following a July 2026 pilot.

The tokenization service is currently integrated with Canton Network and DTCC’s Besu private network, with plans to add additional blockchain networks in 2027.

Tin tức mới nhất được xuất bản vào ngày 28 tháng 10 năm 2026 Nhà cung cấp cơ sở hạ tầng thị trường sau giao dịch cho biết các dịch vụ mã hóa sẽ tạo ra một “con đường thực tế” cho việc áp dụng chứng khoán mã hóa.

Công ty Ủy thác Lưu ký (DTC), một công ty con của Tổng công ty Ủy thác và Thanh toán bù trừ Lưu ký (DTCC), đã triển khai các dịch vụ mã hóa cho phép người dùng đủ điều kiện tạo ra các đại diện mã hóa chứng khoán được nắm giữ tại DTC.

Khách hàng DTCC đủ điều kiện sử dụng Dịch vụ mã thông báo DTCC (DTS). DTS sẽ chuyển đổi giữa các hình thức chứng khoán truyền thống và mã thông báo có thể chuyển nhượng sang ví kỹ thuật số và giữ nguyên quyền sở hữu cũng như bảo vệ nhà đầu tư như các đối tác truyền thống của chúng, công ty đã công bố vào thứ Tư.

Nhà cung cấp cơ sở hạ tầng thị trường sau giao dịch cho biết 20 khách hàng của họ đã ký thỏa thuận truy cập các dịch vụ, bao gồm Alpaca, Citadel Securities, Citi, Clear Street, DriveWealth, Fidelity Investments, Interchange Clearing và JPMorgan.

DTC có hơn 114 nghìn tỷ USD tài sản đang được lưu ký, bao gồm cổ phiếu và quỹ giao dịch trao đổi. Công ty cho biết dịch vụ của họ sẽ tạo ra một “con đường thực tế” cho việc áp dụng chứng khoán được mã hóa.

Vào tháng 12 năm 2025, Ủy ban Chứng khoán và Giao dịch Hoa Kỳ đã ban hành thư “không hành động” tuyên bố rằng họ sẽ không khuyến nghị hành động thực thi đối với công ty con của DTCC liên quan đến chương trình mã thông báo được đề xuất.

Vào tháng 5, DTCC cho biết họ đã lên kế hoạch triển khai đầy đủ dịch vụ giao dịch chứng khoán mã hóa vào tháng 10 năm 2026, sau đợt thí điểm vào tháng 7 năm 2026.

Dịch vụ mã hóa hiện được tích hợp với Mạng riêng Canton Network và Besu của DTCC, với kế hoạch bổ sung thêm các mạng blockchain vào năm 2027.

posts.title: Coinbase Denies Breach After Amplitude Security Incident Exposes Customer Data
posts.titleVi: Coinbase phủ nhận vi phạm sau sự cố bảo mật biên độ làm lộ dữ liệu khách hàng
posts.summary: Coinbase has denied reports of a data breach after a security incident at the third-party analytics vendor Amplitude exposed some customer contact data.
posts.summaryVi: Coinbase đã từ chối các báo cáo về vi phạm dữ liệu sau khi sự cố bảo mật tại nhà cung cấp phân tích bên thứ ba Amplitude làm lộ một số dữ liệu liên hệ của khách hàng.
posts.content:
Coinbase has denied reports of a data breach after a security incident at the third-party analytics vendor Amplitude exposed some customer contact data.

The Nasdaq-listed crypto exchange said a small subset of Coinbase customer information was affected, along with data from other Amplitude customers.

In its official tweet, Coinbase confirmed that there is no evidence of unauthorized access to its systems and that customer funds remain safe. The exchange did not disclose how many users were affected or which specific contact details were exposed. However, exposed email addresses and phone numbers could still put users at risk of phishing and social engineering attacks.

“We are notifying impacted customers and regulatory agencies in accordance with our legal obligations.”

Meanwhile, Amplitude has not yet issued a public statement on how the breach occurred. SlowMist Chief Information Security Officer, “23pds,” claimed that the hackers obtained contact information of more than 70,000 users.

Coinbase is not the only one facing questions over customer data security. South Korea’s second-largest crypto exchange, Bithumb, has reportedly suffered a data leak after an unauthorized outsider accessed one of its internal workplace tools.

According to Yonhap News Agency, Bithumb detected abnormal access to its in-house mobile groupware system on October 27. Some customer personal data was reportedly leaked the following day. The exchange is still working to determine the full scope of the incident. It has not yet confirmed how many customers were affected or which details were exposed.

The incident comes as South Korean financial firms face a series of similar security problems. Daishin Securities reported that information belonging to more than 38,000 customers was leaked. The exposed data reportedly included names, email addresses, and phone numbers. Mirae Asset Global Investment was also affected.

A similar incident happened in September with hardware wallet maker Trezor after a breach involving a third-party provider led to a phishing attempt targeting users. The company warned about a fake email titled “Critical Security Alert: STM32 Entropy Vulnerability” and told users not to click any links. The message falsely claimed a flaw in STM32 microcontrollers could put wallet recovery phrases at risk, even suggesting 25% of devices might be affected.

Trezor said it had taken down the phishing domain and was investigating how attackers accessed its legitimate domain.

posts.contentVi:
Coinbase đã từ chối các báo cáo về vi phạm dữ liệu sau khi sự cố bảo mật tại nhà cung cấp phân tích bên thứ ba Amplitude làm lộ một số dữ liệu liên hệ của khách hàng.

Sàn giao dịch tiền điện tử được niêm yết trên Nasdaq cho biết một tập hợp nhỏ thông tin khách hàng của Coinbase đã bị ảnh hưởng, cùng với dữ liệu từ các khách hàng Amplitude khác.

Trong tweet chính thức của mình, Coinbase xác nhận rằng không có bằng chứng nào về việc truy cập trái phép vào hệ thống của mình và tiền của khách hàng vẫn được an toàn. Sàn giao dịch không tiết lộ có bao nhiêu người dùng bị ảnh hưởng hoặc chi tiết liên hệ cụ thể nào bị lộ. Tuy nhiên, địa chỉ email và số điện thoại bị lộ vẫn có thể khiến người dùng có nguy cơ bị tấn công lừa đảo và tấn công kỹ thuật xã hội.

“Chúng tôi đang thông báo cho các khách hàng và cơ quan quản lý bị ảnh hưởng theo nghĩa vụ pháp lý của chúng tôi.”

Trong khi đó, Amplitude vẫn chưa đưa ra tuyên bố công khai về việc vi phạm xảy ra như thế nào. Giám đốc An ninh Thông tin của SlowMist, “23pds,” tuyên bố rằng tin tặc đã lấy được thông tin liên hệ của hơn 70.000 người dùng.

Coinbase không phải là người duy nhất phải đối mặt với câu hỏi về bảo mật dữ liệu của khách hàng. Sàn giao dịch tiền điện tử lớn thứ hai của Hàn Quốc, Bithumb, được cho là đã bị rò rỉ dữ liệu sau khi một người ngoài trái phép truy cập vào một trong những công cụ làm việc nội bộ của sàn này.

Theo Hãng thông tấn Yonhap, Bithumb đã phát hiện quyền truy cập bất thường vào hệ thống phần mềm nhóm di động nội bộ của mình vào ngày 27 tháng 10. Một số dữ liệu cá nhân của khách hàng được cho là đã bị rò rỉ vào ngày hôm sau. Sàn giao dịch vẫn đang làm việc để xác định toàn bộ phạm vi của vụ việc. Hiện vẫn chưa xác nhận có bao nhiêu khách hàng bị ảnh hưởng hoặc chi tiết nào bị lộ.

Vụ việc xảy ra trong bối cảnh các công ty tài chính Hàn Quốc phải đối mặt với hàng loạt vấn đề bảo mật tương tự. Daishin Securities đưa tin thông tin của hơn 38.000 khách hàng đã bị rò rỉ. Dữ liệu bị lộ được báo cáo bao gồm tên, địa chỉ email và số điện thoại. Mirae Asset Global Investment cũng bị ảnh hưởng.

Một sự cố tương tự đã xảy ra vào tháng 9 với nhà sản xuất ví phần cứng Trezor sau khi vi phạm liên quan đến nhà cung cấp bên thứ ba dẫn đến nỗ lực lừa đảo nhắm mục tiêu vào người dùng. Công ty đã cảnh báo về một email giả mạo có tiêu đề “Cảnh báo bảo mật quan trọng: Lỗ hổng Entropy STM32” và yêu cầu người dùng không nhấp vào bất kỳ liên kết nào. Thông báo tuyên bố sai sự thật về một lỗ hổng trong bộ vi điều khiển STM32 có thể gây nguy hiểm cho các cụm từ khôi phục ví, thậm chí còn cho thấy 25% thiết bị có thể bị ảnh hưởng.

Trezor cho biết họ đã gỡ bỏ miền lừa đảo và đang điều tra cách những kẻ tấn công truy cập vào miền hợp pháp của nó.

Chayanika đã làm phóng viên tài chính được bảy năm. Tốt nghiệp ngành Khoa học Chính trị và Báo chí, mối quan tâm của cô nằm ở ý nghĩa pháp lý với trọng tâm là sự phát triển công nghệ trong lĩnh vực tiền điện tử.

posts.content:
Robinhood now makes more money from predicting the future than trading crypto

The brokerage earned $173 million from event contracts against $120 million from crypto, marking a striking reversal as its digital asset revenue plunged 55%.

By Oluwapelumi Adejumo Senior Reporter • CryptoSlate

01 Robinhood's crypto revenue plunged 55% to $120 million in Q3, falling behind the $173 million generated by prediction markets. 02 Crypto's share of Robinhood's total revenue shrank from 21% to 8.4%, while options and prediction markets powered record company earnings. 03 Robinhood Chain contributed $26 million, masking a 6% quarterly decline in the rest of its crypto business despite rising trading volumes. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Robinhood's cryptocurrency revenue fell 55% in the third quarter, even as its new blockchain helped offset declining trading income.

The brokerage reported $120 million in crypto revenue for the three months ended Sept. 30, trailing the $173 million generated by prediction-market contracts. Meanwhile, total company revenue rose 12% to a record $1.42 billion.

The results highlight a growing divergence between Robinhood's digital asset business and its other trading products, with options and prediction markets emerging as larger revenue contributors.

Robinhood Chain offsets declining crypto trading revenue

According to Robinhood's earnings presentation , its Ethereum-based Layer 2 network, Robinhood Chain, generated more than $50 million in transaction fees during its first quarter on mainnet, contributing $26 million to the company's reported crypto revenue.

The network processed more than $80 billion in decentralized exchange trading volume during the period, ranking among the five largest blockchains by revenue and trading activity, according to Robinhood.

Tom Wan, head of data at Entropy Advisors, noted that Robinhood Chain accounted for approximately 22% of the company's cryptocurrency revenue, generating more than four times Bitstamp's $6 million contribution.

Without the blockchain business, Robinhood's crypto revenue would have declined 6% quarter over quarter to $94 million. Instead, the additional $26 million lifted total crypto revenue 20% from the preceding quarter.

The weakness persisted despite a recovery in trading activity. Cryptocurrency volumes increased 23% sequentially to $49.8 billion, with Bitstamp contributing $29.2 billion and Robinhood's retail application generating $20.6 billion.

However, compared with the same period last year, total crypto trading volume fell 38%. Activity on Robinhood's retail app fell 48%, while Bitstamp's volume contracted 28%. It explained:

“Crypto Notional Trading Volumes decreased 38% year-over-year to $50 billion, including Robinhood App Notional Volumes which decreased 48% year-over-year to $21 billion, and Bitstamp Notional Volumes which decreased 28% year-over-year to $29 billion.”

Robinhood's app generated $88 million in crypto trading revenue, down from $94 million in the second quarter, while Bitstamp's contribution remained unchanged at $6 million.

The decline reduced cryptocurrency's share of Robinhood's overall revenue to 8.4%, down from about 21% a year earlier.

Prediction markets and options drive Robinhood's growth

The cryptocurrency downturn contrasted with accelerating activity across Robinhood's derivatives and equities businesses.

Prediction-market revenue increased more than sixfold year over year to $173 million, surpassing cryptocurrency trading as the platform's second-largest transaction-based revenue category.

Customers traded a record 16.4 billion event contracts during the quarter, more than seven times the volume recorded a year earlier.

Options remained Robinhood's largest transaction-based revenue source, generating $399 million, up 31% annually. The company also reported a record 905 million options contracts traded, up 48%.

Equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million, supported by a 53% increase in trading volume to a record $992 billion.

Together, the gains lifted transaction-based revenue 19% to $867 million, despite the substantial contraction in cryptocurrency revenue.

Wan identified prediction markets and options as Robinhood's principal growth engines, while describing Robinhood Chain as the business responsible for the sequential improvement in crypto revenue.

The broader revenue gains did not translate into higher quarterly profits. Net income fell 14% to $476 million, while diluted earnings per share declined 16% to $0.51.

Robinhood also reported 28.7 million funded customers, up 7% from a year earlier, and $396 billion in platform assets, up 19%.

The company's prediction-market expansion continued through Rothera, its joint venture with Susquehanna International Group, which exceeded $100 million in annualized revenue during its first full quarter of operations.

Robinhood Misses, But Crypto Beats and the Chain Surprises

Robinhood missed on both revenue and EPS on Tuesday, despite crypto beating expectations. But the more interesting things happened on the call.

Revenue came in at a record $1.42 billion, a hair under the $1.43 billion expected. EPS was $0.51 against $0.55 forecast. Crypto revenue rose to $120 million from $100 million in Q2 , up 20% sequentially, though still 55% below last year’s $268 million. Trading volume was $50 billion, with $29 billion of that through Bitstamp.

Event contracts are now the bigger business: $173 million, up from $156 million, on a record 16.4 billion contracts traded, more than seven times a year ago. Between prediction markets and crypto, more than a fifth of Robinhood’s revenue now comes from products that barely existed two years ago.

And then came the call and Vlad’s commentary on Robinhood Chain.

Vlad admitted that Robinhood Chain has outrun their internal forecasts and expectations. The chain launched July 1. By late August it was generating more fees over a rolling 30 days than Ethereum or Base. Tenev said they’ve had to staff up a team to keep pace, and that builders have been telling them Robinhood could be doing more.

His response: “ You should expect to see us really ramping the investment, because you just don’t see growth of a new ecosystem like this. It’s an uncommon thing. A lot of chains have launched over the past few months that have had an incomparably small level of traction compared to this. So we’re doubling down.”

Then he described where he thinks it goes: “Imagine if you take a stock token, make it fully programmable just like software. What can you do? Can you have tokenized options contracts?”

This was music to the Robinhood Chain bulls’ ears. And it was enough to send the Robinhood Chain leaders up 20-50% across the board, led by Pons +18%, AI (Long) +33% and Orbio +57%.

The message was clear. Robinhood isn’t treating tokenized equities as a product feature, it’s treating them as a primitive other people build on top of. That’s already happening with projects like Long.xyz pairing meme coins against tokenized NVDA and TSLA and Orbio funding AI inference credits with fees paid in tokenized Nvidia. Neither was Robinhood’s idea, and both only exist because the stock tokens do.

Now those teams can expect more support from the Robinhood team. Two tweets from Robinhood Crypto on Tuesday already evidence this leaning in, supporting both Long and Priors . So earnings may have been a miss, but the earnings call was a big win. Now let’s see just what leaning in means…

[PRESS RELEASE – Willemstad, Curaçao, October 27th, 2026]

BetFury , a leading crypto casino, is officially marking its seventh Anniversary with Birthday 007 . The platform-wide campaign is styled after the world of secret agents and backed by a guaranteed $2,000,000 prize pool. The event brings a four-day announcement phase on October 26, 2026, followed by the main spy operation running from October 30 to November 14, 2026. Transforming players into elite secret agents, BetFury offers an exclusive run of high-reward birthday assignments.

The event runs on BetFury with several promotions in parallel. It starts with “Make Some Fury” Giveaway and the Birthday Raffle. After that, the event will gain momentum along with Agent Missions, Birthday Wheel Drops, the Grand Tournament, the Secret Bonus Roulette, the Sharp Prediction Event, and FunFury Agents Battles.

Users can earn tickets to the Birthday Raffle simply by playing games on the platform, placing bets, and making deposits. These tickets grant entry into the lottery, which runs across a four-day announcement phase from October 26 to October 30. The activity features a guaranteed $100,000 prize pool paid out entirely in BFG tokens, which will be distributed among 300 winning places.

$1,400,000 Birthday Battles and Grand Tournament

Competition sits at the center of the event. The Birthday Battles run on a $1,000,000 progressive prize pool across Original Games, Slots, Sports, and Live Casino . Alongside them, the Grand Tournament is the headline leaderboard race, adding another $400,000 for the agents who climb highest.

Agent Missions launch as the event’s headline operation, plunging players into a high-stakes tactical campaign. All classified assignments are dynamically tailored to a player’s Rank. They feature dedicated operations for Rank 1, Ranks 2-4, Ranks 5-9, and Rank 10+, ensuring a fair, calibrated, and highly competitive battlefield for every operative.

The Secret Bonus Roulette grants all users a daily reward accessible via a simple spin upon logging in. Resetting every day at 12:00 UTC, each sealed pack delivers a variety of Free Spins, Dice Free Spins, Free Bets, or No Risk Bets. These daily bonuses can be deployed in-game, enabling players to consistently progress in both ongoing battles and tournaments.

Three further promotions round out the operation. Birthday Wheel Drops, run in partnership with Pragmatic Play , add in-game prize drops across participating titles. The Sharp Prediction Event covers football , basketball, and more, with a $10,000 pool for correct calls before kick-off. And the FunFury Agents Battle runs free for the full event, with improved terms for the birthday.

“Seven years is a milestone most platforms mark with a banner and a bonus,” said Mike, CEO of BetFury. “We turned ours into a full operation. Every part of Birthday 007 is a thank-you to the players who got us here, and the scale of it is the clearest way we know to say it.”

Users can visit the main event page to take part in Birthday 007.

Established in 2019, BetFury is a leading crypto casino with over 3.5M registered players and $11.5B in lifetime wagering volume. The platform offers over 13,000 games, including 24 Original games with an RTP of up to 99.28%, and 80+ sports for betting with highly competitive market odds. Beyond gaming, BetFury provides a full suite of advanced crypto utilities, including Crypto Staking with up to 60% APR, Futures, and Crypto Swap. Moreover, the platform features proprietary BFG Staking, enabling users to hold native tokens to earn daily passive payouts in either BFG or USDT. BetFury continuously evolves based on user feedback and remains deeply committed to responsible gambling practices.

Crypto Daybook Americas Dissent and more: 3 things to watch for at the Fed meeting

By Omkar Godbole | Edited by Sheldon Reback Oct 28, 2026, 7:57 a.m. EDT

3 min read Make preferred on Share 

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images) Summary Show This is an excerpt from CoinDesk newsletter 'Daybook.' Sign up here , if you haven't already.

The Federal Reserve will announce its interest-rate decision at 2 p.m. ET (18:00 UTC), followed by Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference half an hour later.

Here are key themes to watch for that may influence interest-rate expectations and markets.

Dissent: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) is expected to keep the benchmark interest rate unchanged in the 3.75%–4% range. That outcome has been widely anticipated since the September projections, when most officials penciled in just one more rate increase this year, with December seen as the most likely timing.

That makes any dissent particularly significant. If three or more voting members opposed holding rates steady and instead favored raising, that would signal growing urgency among policymakers to tighten policy and fuel expectations of more aggressive hikes in the coming months. That could bolster the Dollar Index and potentially weigh on bitcoin BTC $80,690.83 .

Comments on financial conditions: The 10-year Treasury yield has pulled back to 5%, a 36 basis-point drop since Oct. 7. The 30-year yield has declined by 40 bps. This has eased financial conditions, which track credit availability in the economy, with a knock-on effect on risk-taking in financial markets. If Warsh acknowledges this easing, it could amp up bets on rate increases in the coming months.

Warsh’s comments on inflation: Consumer price inflation has come in above expectations for two consecutive months. Oil prices remain elevated near $100, and U.S. diesel prices are at record highs. Warsh’s thoughts on the subject could influence the market. Moreover, high energy prices provide little room for him to express bias for growth over inflation.

Bitcoin is rising before the meeting. It was recently trading at $81,411, up more than 2% over 24 hours. Ether ETH $2,342.29 , solana (SOL) and XRP (XRP) have also gained more than 2%.

posts.content:
All financial eyes today will be on the highly anticipated US Federal Reserve FOMC meeting, as its conclusion will shed more light on the central bank’s monetary policy views.

Aside from the immediate impact on the financial markets after the interest rate decision is announced, investors will pay special attention to Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s speech shortly after the meeting.

The primary cryptocurrency tends to move quite sporadically in the days and hours leading up to the latest FOMC meetings. The past 24 hours have been rather positive for the asset, as it climbed from under $79,500 to $81,700 before it was stopped. Ali Martinez commented on this price uptick and outlined a bearish scenario for bitcoin once the meeting concludes.

“In the FOMC meetings I’ve tracked, Bitcoin’s first-hour move has often been less than 1%. A clearer direction tends to emerge over the next 24 hours and has often persisted a week later.”

He added that this history makes today’s price movement even more important, but warned that the current on-chain signals give him “reason to be cautious.” First, he noted that BTC whales have realized over $150 million in profits in just a few days. Their holdings have declined by more than 8,160 BTC in 24 hours, which is equivalent to $664 million.

“That decline suggests large holders are reducing exposure ahead of the decision.”

The Coinbase Premium Index remains in negative territory, hitting a monthly low at -0.17. This signals that US investors remain on the sidelines or are actually in a sell mode. Martinez warned that bitcoin now trades above the key $81,000 support, where almost a million units previously changed hands. If it breaks decisively to the downside, he expects a drop to $77,000 or perhaps even $67,000.

To invalidate this bearish thesis, the cryptocurrency would have to break past $84,500, where 620,000 units traded. If it does, then the door toward $92,000 and $104,000 opens wide.

The FOMC meeting is one of the most notable macro events of the week, with experts anticipating no interest rate changes. Although the CPI and PPI data from earlier this month showed inflation is still very persistent and above the Fed’s 2% target, markets are reportedly “bracing for a Fed pause” after last month’s first hike in over three years.

However, Kevin Warsh’s post-FOMC speech could be even more important for BTC’s price. While experts believe there will be no hike now, they warned that the Fed could hike rates once again in December.

Jordan got into crypto in 2016 by trading and investing. He began writing about blockchain technology in 2017 and now serves as CryptoPotato's Assistant Editor-in-Chief. He has managed numerous crypto-related projects and is passionate about all things blockchain.

Tech XRP Ledger developers propose creating wallets with zero XRP for stablecoin payments

An experimental change would let companies cover the reserve for customer and AI-agent accounts, allowing users to start with stablecoins without first acquiring XRP.

By Shaurya Malwa Oct 28, 2026, 7:52 a.m. EDT

2 min read Make preferred on Share 

XRP Ledger developers propose creating wallets with zero XRP for stablecoin payments. (Jonas Lupe/Unsplash) Summary Show XRP Ledger developers are testing a transaction that would let sponsors cover account reserves, allowing new wallets to hold zero XRP. The proposal could reduce costs for payment applications and automated software by enabling sponsors to pay users’ reserve requirements and transaction fees without controlling their private keys. The code remains under review and depends on a broader sponsorship amendment that had secured only 11 of the 29 validator votes required for approval as of Oct. 19.

Developers working on the XRP Ledger are testing a way to create blockchain accounts with zero XRP in them, potentially allowing payment applications and automated software to operate without first depositing the cryptocurrency into every wallet.

A code proposal submitted Oct. 15 introduces a transaction called SponsoredAccountCreate , which would allow an existing account to create another account and cover its reserve requirement.

XRP Ledger currently requires a minimum reserve of 1 XRP for each account. That money remains locked while the account is active, preventing the network from being flooded with empty wallets.

A company creating 100,000 separate accounts would need to set aside 100,000 XRP just to meet those reserve requirements.

Under the proposed system, a sponsoring account would cover the reserve, allowing the new wallet to keep a zero XRP balance. The network’s overall reserve obligation would remain, with the sponsor carrying the cost instead of the customer.

Sponsors could also cover transaction fees through a broader sponsorship mechanism, allowing applications to pay those charges on behalf of their users.

Ripple recently partnered with Stripe-owned Privy to bring embedded wallets to XRP Ledger applications. The integration is intended to support payments using XRP and Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin, including automated payments made by AI agents.

Those wallets currently need XRP funding before they can become active, even when they’re only meant to hold stablecoins.

The proposed account-creation transaction builds on the broader Sponsored Fees and Reserves standard, which allows another account to pay network costs without taking control of the user’s private keys. The new code would create an account directly without sending it any XRP.

The pull request remains open , with two unresolved automated code-review findings. It also depends on sponsorship changes that have yet to activate on mainnet.

Those changes still need validator approval. The sponsorship amendment had 11 of the 35 votes it needs from the network’s trusted validators as of Oct. 19, according to XRPL Dashboard , well short of the 29 required.

SUN.io Completes 52nd Buyback and Burn: Total SUN Burned Surpasses 685M as SunSwap Accelerates Ecosystem Integrations

Through its recurring buyback and burn program, SUN.io continues to channel protocol revenue from SunSwap, SunPump, and SunX into SUN token value accrual, while accelerating SunSwap's cross-platform integrations to reinforce decentralized liquidity.

Published Oct. 28, 2026 Updated Oct. 28, 2026

SUN.io, the core DeFi liquidity infrastructure on the TRON network, has successfully executed its 52nd SUN token buyback and burn on October 27, removing more than 7.23 million SUN from circulation.

This round marks the platform's 52nd consecutive burn, bringing the cumulative total to over 685 million SUN tokens, valued at more than $11 million. The recurring, uninterrupted buybacks and burn cycle steadily reduces the circulating supply of SUN, underscoring the protocol's long-term commitment to sustainable ecosystem growth.

To guarantee complete on-chain transparency, SUN.io has launched a dedicated public dashboard for its SUN token buyback and burn program. The portal provides real-time access to program design, key metrics, funding sources, and detailed on-chain records for each burn round, enabling community members to verify the data at any time.

Alongside the ecosystem value accrual from its periodic token burns, SUN.io is rapidly expanding its product footprint—most notably through strategic integrations with its flagship DEX, SunSwap. The platform has recently completed full-stack technical integrations and formed deep strategic partnerships with on-chain trading aggregator Ave.ai, leading multi-chain wallet TokenPocket, and cross-chain liquidity protocol Symbiosis.

These partnerships not only broaden SunSwap's user reach and unlock the potential of its underlying DEX architecture, but also deliver more affordable token swapping and liquidity services with fewer frictions for DeFi participants across the broader TRON ecosystem.

685M+ SUN Burned: Building a Traceable Value Loop Across the SUN Ecosystem

Since the launch of its buyback and burn program in 2021, SUN.io has maintained a consistent execution schedule across multiple market cycles. The first 52 burn rounds executed so far have removed up to 700 million SUN from circulation—representing over $11 million in value and approximately 3.44% of the total token supply. This outstanding track record has helped mitigate the impact of short-term market volatility while rallying SUN holders and ecosystem builders under a clear, dependable value thesis and sustainable roadmap.

According to the Announcement on the 52nd SUN Token Buyback and Burn (July 25, 2026—October 25, 2026), SUN.io executed 7,232,977.17 SUN (over 7.23 million SUN) during this time period.

The cumulative burn volume since the initial round on December 15, 2021 has surpassed the 685 million mark to 685,780,165.49 SUN.

All capital deployed for the buyback was funded by protocol revenues generated across SUN.io's three core verticals. Burn contributions by vertical are:

SunSwap V2: 388,023,868.41 SUN SunPump: 285,879,914.81 SUN SunX: 11,876,382.27 SUN This multi-stream composition demonstrates that value capture spans the full SUN.io ecosystem. As protocol revenues generated across SunSwap V2, SunPump, and SunX are continuously channeled into the buyback and burn reserve, organic growth in any single vertical translates into direct support for the token's value accrual.

This creates a self-reinforcing flywheel where ecosystem revenue growth continues to fuel protocol buybacks, which in turn contract circulating supply and drive long-term token value accrual.

Every buyback operation adheres strictly to on-chain transparency standards, with transaction hashes for each execution indexed publicly to guarantee a traceable, verifiable paper trail for community audit.

On top of this, the platform's dedicated SUN Buyback & Burn dashboard further institutionalizes the commitment to transparency by centralizing core metrics, execution workflows, revenue allocation breakdown, and historical on-chain transaction records. It shows cumulative burn volumes, upcoming burn accruals, execution rules, and revenue allocations across all verticals. With every historical transaction mapped directly to on-chain addresses for verification, the entire buyback and burn process remains subject to ongoing community audit, reinforcing trust in the platform's transparent value loop.

Backed by verifiable on-chain records and real-time reporting on the official SUN Buyback & Burn dashboard, SUN.io is delivering on its multi-cycle deflationary commitment through radical transparency. By establishing an unbroken, auditable pipeline—routing protocol revenue directly into permanent token burns—the platform reinforces predictable, long-term value accrual for SUN holders.

Live metrics from the dashboard confirm that cumulative on-chain burns have crossed 685 million SUN (approx. $11 million), permanently retiring 3.44% of the total circulating supply. Meanwhile, buyback momentum remains strong, with the latest cycle securing an additional 7.1 million SUN ready for burning.

As the SUN.io ecosystem scales, protocol revenue streams expand alongside it, strengthening the reserve earmarked for future buybacks. This sustained, fully transparent value-return loop provides a robust foundation for the token's long-term value accrual.

SunSwap Accelerates Ecosystem Integrations to Fuel Growth Across TRON's DeFi Landscape

Alongside the continuous rollout of its buyback and burn program, SUN.io is ramping up its product expansion and ecosystem infrastructure. SunSwap, the platform's core DEX, has made significant headway in its strategic partner program, completing end-to-end technical integrations with on-chain trading aggregator Ave.ai, leading multi-chain wallet TokenPocket, and cross-chain liquidity protocol Symbiosis.

These partnerships span three core dimensions: aggregated trading entry points, high-traffic wallet access, and cross-chain liquidity routing. Together, they expand SunSwap's user reach, giving TRON DeFi users lower-friction access to deep liquidity and seamless token swaps.

The SUN.io team is actively onboarding more third-party platforms, extending SunSwap's integration footprint across a broader array of Web3 consumer touchpoints.

The platform's core operating metrics exhibit the same momentum. As of October 26, on-chain data shows SunSwap's total value locked (TVL) approaching $645 million across more than 26,800 active liquidity pools. Network throughput remains steady, with daily on-chain transactions topping 14,000 and average daily trading volume holding above $50 million—solidifying the ecosystem's leadership in the industry.

Growth extends beyond SunSwap, with SUN.io's broader product suite maintaining sharp upward momentum—most notably across its derivatives arm. According to DeFiLlama, total trading volume across all SUN.io product lines approached $15 billion in Q3 2026. Spot DEX trading contributed over $5 billion, while perpetual contract (perp) volume neared $9.7 billion, up roughly 25% quarter-over-quarter from the ~$7.75 billion performance in Q2.

The combined progress of SunSwap's ecosystem integrations and multi-product volume growth points to a broader shift: SUN.io's full-stack liquidity infrastructure now serves a much wider range of on-chain trading needs beyond spot trading, creating a DeFi product matrix where multiple business lines grow in tandem.

On the incentives front, JustLend, the lending platform in the JUST ecosystem, joined forces in July with core TRON-based projects and Binance Web3 Wallet to roll out the $4.5 million TRON DeFi Summer campaign. Participants who supply liquidity to the dedicated SUN pool on JustLend can earn additional boosted yields. The campaign is currently running Season 3 (S3), where APYs in the SUN pool reach up to 25%, offering users a compelling option to co-build ecosystem liquidity while earning on-chain returns.

Between the token-burn feedback loop, volume expansion across core business lines, and active partner-incentive campaigns, SUN.io is activating a clear growth flywheel: infrastructure upgrades drive transaction volume, business growth feeds value back to users, and that value attracts further ecosystem expansion.

Looking ahead, SUN.io, as core DeFi liquidity infrastructure for the TRON ecosystem, plans to continue its buyback and burn program, channeling protocol revenue generated by ecosystem growth into the underlying value of the SUN token. On the product side, the platform will continue securing cross-platform integrations, deepening SunSwap's liquidity, refining the end-to-end user experience, and broadening its product lineup. With ecosystem partners on board, SUN.io will keep expanding its cross-platform integrations and deliver transparent and efficient infrastructure that supports the long-term on-chain growth of TRON DeFi and the diverse trading needs of users worldwide.

Written by Zoltan Vardai staff writer Edited by Yohan Yun staff editor Written by Zoltan Vardai staff writer Edited by Yohan Yun staff editor

Settlement concerns prompt Euronext to halt CoinShares’ Zcash ETP ahead of debut

Latest News Published Oct 28, 2026 A Euronext spokesperson told Cointelegraph the suspension was due to “operational settlement requirements” and remains in effect until settlement operations are supported by the CSD.

Stock exchange operator Euronext suspended CoinShares’ Zcash exchange-traded product (ETP) on Wednesday, when it was scheduled to debut for trading on Euronext Paris.

In a Wednesday notice , the exchange operator said the CoinShares Zcash ETP (ZCSH) was suspended from trading on Euronext Paris until further notice. The notice did not provide a reason for the decision.

CoinShares’ Zcash ETP will remain suspended until “standard settlement operations can be fully supported by the Central Securities Depository (CSD),” Euronext’s press and communications manager, Flavio Bornancin-Tomasella, told Cointelegraph, adding that the measure was strictly limited to “operational settlement requirements.”

The suspension notice delays what would have been the fourth Zcash-based ETP listed in Europe. Other companies that launched Zcash ETPs earlier this year include 21Shares, Virtune and Valor.

CoinShares announced the planned launch of its ZCASH ETP on Euronext Paris earlier on Wednesday. Cointelegraph contacted CoinShares for comment on the matter but did not receive a response by publication.

posts.content:
6 minutes ago · 8:40 a.m. EDT Stephen Alpher

Share Share this post 

Robinhood slumps 6% after underwhelming results; Coinbase slips 2%

“We've been tracking every broker/exchange that has reported Q3 and the obvious weak link is pricing,” wrote Matthew Siegel , head of digital assets research at Van Eck. “Robinhood HOOD continued that today with weak-ish pricing power across options, equities and crypto.”

Read more: Robinhood's crypto revenue fell 55% from last year, but topped Street forecasts

Plugging each of his brokerage earnings summaries into Claude, Siegel got this result: “Unit pricing is the weak link. Rates and FX products have the best mix of volume and price, helped by the rate backdrop. Everything driven by retail or micro-sized flow is growing volume but not revenue due to weakening pricing.”

HOOD is lower by 6.3% pre-market. Coinbase COIN — which reports its third-quarter results on Thursday — is down 2%.

Written by Yohan Yun staff editor Edited by Robert Lakin staff editor Written by Yohan Yun staff editor Edited by Robert Lakin staff editor

Mirae Asset Securities issues tokenized notes on Solana

Latest News Published Oct 28, 2026 The company’s Hong Kong unit issued six-month notes under its $3 billion program, extending blockchain-based distribution to institutional investors.

The Hong Kong arm of Mirae Asset Securities, one of South Korea’s largest securities firms, has issued tokenized notes on Solana to institutional investors.

The transaction involved six-month floating-rate notes issued under the firm’s $3 billion structured note program, according to Wednesday’s announcement . Singapore-based digital market infrastructure operator Marketnode acted as an authorized distributor.

Mirae Asset Securities managed token issuance, payments and the notes’ lifecycle using its internal digital infrastructure. The company said the transaction could provide a model for distributing a wider range of structured products through blockchain-based channels.

The securities firm is part of South Korea’s Mirae Asset Financial Group, whose businesses span brokerage, investment banking, asset management and insurance.

The group has been expanding into digital assets, with affiliate Mirae Asset Consulting acquiring a controlling stake in crypto exchange Korbit in July, which has since rebranded to Digital X .

The group’s asset management arm, Mirae Asset Global Investments, operates the Global X and TIGER exchange-traded fund brands. Its website lists $275 billion in ETF assets under management as of June 2026 and describes its ETF business as the world’s 12th-largest.

The group has been expanding into digital assets, with affiliate Mirae Asset Consulting acquiring a controlling stake in crypto exchange Korbit in July, which has since rebranded to Digital X .

The group’s asset management arm, Mirae Asset Global Investments, operates the Global X and TIGER exchange-traded fund brands. Its website lists $275 billion in ETF assets under management as of June 2026 and describes its ETF business as the world’s 12th-largest.

Bitcoin beats the S&P 500 on most trading days but still loses the month

Bitcoin outperformed US stocks in 10 of 18 October sessions, but losses twice as large as its winning margins left it trailing as BlackRock dominated ETF inflows.

By Gino Matos Reporter • CryptoSlate

01 Bitcoin beat the S&P on 56% of October sessions, yet fell 4.25% as losing days hit harder. 02 IBIT captured 96.3% of US spot Bitcoin ETF inflows since August as rivals saw redemptions. 03 Weak spot demand, lower stablecoin supply and downside hedging leave Bitcoin’s recovery fragile. Make CryptoSlate preferred on Share

Bitcoin's relative win rate against the S&P 500 recovered above 50% in recent sessions, up from about one session in five in June, its weakest stretch in roughly six years, according to Glassnode.

Coinbase Institutional's Oct. 23 report found BlackRock's IBIT drawing about $6 billion since Aug. 1 against roughly $500 million across all other US spot Bitcoin ETFs, a 92% share of net inflows. Farside Investors’ data extended through Oct. 26 puts the share at 96.3%.

A date-matched calculation for October through Oct. 26 shows Bitcoin beating the S&P 500 on 10 of 18 sessions (55.6%). Bitcoin fell 4.25% over the same stretch, and the S&P rose 0.33%, a 4.58% gap in stocks' favor.

In its 10 winning sessions, Bitcoin's average edge was about 0.71%, and in its eight losing sessions, its average shortfall was 1.44%, roughly twice as large.

In the first half of 2026, corporate treasuries bought about $14.5 billion of Bitcoin while US spot ETFs saw almost $5 billion of net outflows. Since August, ETFs have drawn roughly $6.4 billion against about $1.5 billion from treasuries.

Farside Investors’ fund-level data shows that from Aug. 3 through Oct. 26, IBIT took in a net $5.7 billion and every other fund combined $221 million.

October's share is undefined as a concentration measure, since IBIT added $866 million while rival funds lost over $1 billion and the whole category sits at about $203 million of net outflows.

The Farside figure through Oct. 21 was about 90.5%, so the rise toward 96.3% reflects redemptions at other funds as much as buying at IBIT.

Across October's 18 sessions, IBIT averaged $48.1 million of daily net inflows and competing funds lost $59.4 million a day, for a combined daily outflow of $11.3 million.

If rival redemptions held that pace, IBIT's daily inflows would need to rise about 24%, to $59.4 million, to bring the category to zero.

Concentration describes the observable ETF channel, and IBIT serves many investors, advisers and market makers.

ETF creations and redemptions pass through hedging, inventory and settlement before reaching the spot market, so the share measures ETF flows and leaves single buyers and total Bitcoin purchases outside its scope.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

Stablecoin supply sits about $12.7 billion below its May peak, and the seven-day Coinbase premium stayed negative through October, as of the Oct. 23 report, pointing to soft US spot demand.

Glassnode's latest weekly report shows spot cumulative volume delta at negative $80.5 million, futures open interest near $37.5 billion, and active addresses near 615,200. Options 25-delta skew climbed to 10.4% from 8.9%, which shows stronger demand for downside protection.

Stablecoin supply is a liquidity stock, the premium compares two venues, and open interest counts positions on both sides. Together, they describe a regulated-access bid firmer than the underlying spot market.

Related Reading Bitcoin’s failed breakout reveals a dangerous mix of thin volume and easy profits

Glassnode's Oct. 7 research noted that seven-day spot and ETF volume of about $6.8 billion was lower than on roughly 90% of days since January 2024, and identifiable new inflows covered less than two-fifths of the 30-day rise in realized capitalization.

Higher prices can reflect existing coins changing hands at higher valuations.

If the Fed holds, December expectations hold steady, IBIT inflows continue, and rival funds return to inflows, Bitcoin has a path from the $81,300 ETF cost basis Coinbase cites toward $82,500 to $84,400.

A move toward $88,000 to $95,000 would need the macro burden to ease and the dollar to soften. A falling IBIT share would be a constructive reading if it reflected competitors attracting inflows, and a worse reading if IBIT itself lost demand faster than other funds.

If strong GDP or sticky PCE reinforces higher-for-longer rates while IBIT inflows fade and other ETFs keep losing assets, a break below $77,000 to $77,800 would expose the $73,000 to $75,000 zone Coinbase identifies.

One-month implied volatility near 35%, in the bottom 7th percentile since 2019, frames the range. A one-standard-deviation move is roughly 4.8% either way over seven days, or about $76,100 to $83,900 from the $80,007 close on Oct. 26, and about 10% over 30 days.

Bitcoin's winning days are returning, and one fund drives the demand behind them. Net flows at rival ETFs, stablecoin supply, and the Coinbase premium will show whether the recovery broadens.

Tech Google to preview crypto custody security system as AI threats grow

Google Multi-Party Compute is in private preview, with several major financial institutions testing the technology and parent company Alphabet using it to secure its own digital assets on Ethereum and Solana.

By Aoyon Ashraf | Edited by Nikhilesh De Updated Oct 28, 2026, 8:35 a.m. EDT Published Oct 28, 2026, 7:00 a.m. EDT

6 min read Make preferred on Share 

Google testing crypto security system as private-key hacks mount. (Karollyne Videira Hubert/Unsplash) 摘要 显示 Google will unveil a security service that uses multi-party computation to help financial institutions safeguard and transfer cryptocurrencies and tokenized assets, with commercial availability planned for early 2027. The system distributes private-key fragments across separate environments and applies institutional rules before transactions are signed, reducing the risk that one compromised machine could expose assets. Google says the service can eventually support post-quantum cryptography, but its current protections focus on compromised credentials and unauthorized transactions amid billions of dollars in private-key-related thefts.

Google is set to showcase a new security system designed to help banks and other financial institutions safeguard and move cryptocurrencies and tokenized assets at its inaugural digital assets symposium in New York City on Wednesday.

The product, officially named Google Multi-Party Compute (MPC), is in private preview and is not yet generally available. Several design partners and major financial institutions are testing the technology, Google told CoinDesk. Alphabet, the parent company, has also begun using it to secure its own digital assets on the Ethereum and Solana blockchains.

Google did not identify the institutions testing the service or specify which digital assets Alphabet is securing. The company plans to make Google Multi-Party Compute commercially available in early 2027, but has not disclosed pricing.

MPC isn't new to digital assets, nor is Google's involvement in the technology. The i dea is to split a private key into individual fragments and distribute them across multiple separate systems, so there is no single point of failure. In 2023, Google published guidance explaining how customers could build MPC-based digital-asset systems using its Confidential Space infrastructure.

Google said it has not previously offered a dedicated MPC custody product for cryptocurrencies. Its existing production services include Google Cloud Key Management Service (KMS) and Cloud HSM , which institutions use to manage and protect cryptographic keys. The new offering brings MPC-based signing, transaction policies and key recovery into a purpose-built service for digital assets, rather than requiring customers to assemble those capabilities themselves.

The move comes as banks and other financial companies explore using blockchains to issue tokenized assets, process payments and offer digital asset custody services. Those activities require institutions to securely authorize transactions that, once completed on a blockchain, generally cannot be reversed.

“Digital asset adoption and tokenization are at an inflection point. As regulated financial institutions begin adopting blockchains and tokenization, they need scalable, proven infrastructure to secure their clients’ assets," Rich Widmann, director of digital assets strategy at Google Cloud, told CoinDesk.

An attacker who gains control of the private key protecting a wallet may be able to transfer its assets without the owner's permission, making key management a critical security challenge for institutions entering the market.

The threat has already cost the crypto industry billions of dollars over the years. According to blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis, compromised private keys accounted for 43.8% of cryptocurrency stolen in 2024 . Separately, DeFiLlama data showed that as of June of this year, blockchain projects have lost a cumulative $16.69 billion to hacks and exploits, with roughly 40% of those losses attributed to private-key compromises.

Recent examples include stablecoin protocol Resolv, which suffered a March attack involving a compromised private key controlling a privileged account and weaknesses in its minting system, allowing a hacker to extract about $25 million . In June, attackers compromised the private keys of a Humanity Protocol foundation member and drained more than $32 million from at least 17 wallets. The breach also sent the project's token plunging more than 80%, showing how stolen credentials can cause losses beyond the assets directly taken.

The tech giant's new system aims to reduce the risk of relying on a single private key by using "multi-party computation," or MPC, which distributes control of a private key among multiple parties or computers. This way, instead of relying on a single key, the system requires several distinct pieces of cryptographic information to work together to authorize a transaction.

The complete private key is never stored in one place, according to Google, reducing the risk of an attacker taking control of the assets, even if a single machine is compromised. It also said that customers retain control of their key material and that the company cannot access it in unencrypted form, even when key shares are held on Google's infrastructure.

Google is also positioning the service as a response to increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks, including threats involving artificial intelligence (AI) and quantum computing.

AI is already helping some cryptocurrency scammers operate on a larger scale, while researchers warn of potential future threats to the cryptography that protects digital assets.

Chainalysis found that cryptocurrency scams linked to AI-tool vendors extracted an average of $3.2 million per operation in 2025, compared with $719,000 for scams without such links — roughly 4.5 times as much. The findings suggest that AI may be helping fraudsters operate at a greater scale, although the report doesn't establish that AI directly caused the higher proceeds.

Recently, Ethereum researcher Justin Drake warned that advances in AI could eventually uncover mathematical shortcuts that could break the digital signatures protecting Bitcoin and Ethereum wallets. Drake said such a breakthrough could emerge in a worst-case scenario within months rather than years, potentially before sufficiently powerful quantum computers arrive.

No AI system has demonstrated the ability to break the cryptographic signatures that protect Bitcoin or Ethereum wallets. AI systems can be used to uncover flaws in poorly encrypted tools, such as last week's certification authority debacle. Google's current MPC protections address threats such as compromised credentials and unauthorized transactions, rather than a hypothetical breakthrough against the underlying cryptography.

The system can help address existing threats by checking transactions against institutional rules before they are signed, potentially preventing transfers that violate preset limits or approval requirements. Those controls may reduce the risk of unauthorized transactions . However, the risk of legitimate users being deceived into authorizing malicious transactions may still pose a threat.

Quantum computing, although not imminent, poses a distinct, longer-term threat to institutions exploring digital asset adoption.

Google researchers have previously estimated that a sufficiently powerful future quantum computer could theoretically derive a bitcoin private key from an exposed public key in roughly 9 minutes , assuming advanced preparation. While no quantum computer is currently capable of such an attack, about 6.9 million bitcoin have been reported as potentially vulnerable to future quantum attacks because their public keys have been exposed.

Google said its architecture is designed to support future upgrades to post-quantum cryptography, which seeks to protect digital signatures against attacks by sufficiently powerful quantum computers. The company said its MPC offering is designed to support conventional ECDSA and Ed25519 cryptographic signing algorithms at general availability.

Google did not provide a timetable for adding post-quantum signing capabilities but said the upgrades could be introduced as blockchain networks adopt the necessary cryptography, without requiring institutions to redesign their systems or interrupt operations.

A bank, for example, could keep one share of a cryptographic signing key in Google Cloud, another on its own hardware and a third with another cloud provider.

When the bank wants to move assets, the transaction enters Google's Confidential Space, where a policy engine checks it against the institution's rules before signing can begin, according to Google.

Those rules could include limits on the amount being transferred, restrictions on destination wallets and requirements for approval from several departments. The checks run inside Google's Confidential Space technology, which uses hardware-isolated computing environments designed to protect sensitive information from unauthorized access.

Google says the system can also accommodate different cryptographic signing thresholds, such as requiring two of three or five of seven participants to jointly produce a transaction signature.

That flexibility is intended to address a concern for banks: they may want the convenience of cloud infrastructure without giving a single technology provider complete control over the credentials needed to move their assets.

Google said institutions can distribute those credentials across their own hardware, Google Cloud and competing cloud services. The company also said its system supports fast transaction signing and key recovery, although it did not provide independently verified performance comparisons with existing custody products.

Google's planned entry to the market brings one of the world's largest cloud providers closer to competing in a market already served by specialist crypto security firms, including Fireblocks, Fordefi and BitGo, which offer technology to help institutions protect and authorize blockchain transactions.

Google argues that its banking relationships and security expertise give it an edge over specialized crypto custody providers. It also sees an opportunity among banks wary of relying on providers that compete for the same customers, positioning itself as a neutral infrastructure supplier that lets institutions run their own custody businesses.

It's worth noting that Google's entry does not eliminate the need for institutions to assess the risks of their technology providers. Even when signing credentials are distributed across different environments, banks may still depend on Google for parts of

By Aoyon Ashraf | Edited by Nikhilesh De Updated Oct 28, 2026, 8:35 a.m. EDT Published Oct 28, 2026, 7:00 a.m. EDT

6 min read Make preferred on Share 

Google testing crypto security system as private-key hacks mount. (Karollyne Videira Hubert/Unsplash) 摘要 显示 Google will unveil a security service that uses multi-party computation to help financial institutions safeguard and transfer cryptocurrencies and tokenized assets, with commercial availability planned for early 2027. The system distributes private-key fragments across separate environments and applies institutional rules before transactions are signed, reducing the risk that one compromised machine could expose assets. Google says the service can eventually support post-quantum cryptography, but its current protections focus on compromised credentials and unauthorized transactions amid billions of dollars in private-key-related thefts.

Google is set to showcase a new security system designed to help banks and other financial institutions safeguard and move cryptocurrencies and tokenized assets at its inaugural digital assets symposium in New York City on Wednesday.

The product, officially named Google Multi-Party Compute (MPC), is in private preview and is not yet generally available. Several design partners and major financial institutions are testing the technology, Google told CoinDesk. Alphabet, the parent company, has also begun using it to secure its own digital assets on the Ethereum and Solana blockchains.

Google did not identify the institutions testing the service or specify which digital assets Alphabet is securing. The company plans to make Google Multi-Party Compute commercially available in early 2027, but has not disclosed pricing.

MPC isn't new to digital assets, nor is Google's involvement in the technology. The i dea is to split a private key into individual fragments and distribute them across multiple separate systems, so there is no single point of failure. In 2023, Google published guidance explaining how customers could build MPC-based digital-asset systems using its Confidential Space infrastructure.

Google said it has not previously offered a dedicated MPC custody product for cryptocurrencies. Its existing production services include Google Cloud Key Management Service (KMS) and Cloud HSM , which institutions use to manage and protect cryptographic keys. The new offering brings MPC-based signing, transaction policies and key recovery into a purpose-built service for digital assets, rather than requiring customers to assemble those capabilities themselves.

The move comes as banks and other financial companies explore using blockchains to issue tokenized assets, process payments and offer digital asset custody services. Those activities require institutions to securely authorize transactions that, once completed on a blockchain, generally cannot be reversed.

“Digital asset adoption and tokenization are at an inflection point. As regulated financial institutions begin adopting blockchains and tokenization, they need scalable, proven infrastructure to secure their clients’ assets," Rich Widmann, director of digital assets strategy at Google Cloud, told CoinDesk.

An attacker who gains control of the private key protecting a wallet may be able to transfer its assets without the owner's permission, making key management a critical security challenge for institutions entering the market.

The threat has already cost the crypto industry billions of dollars over the years. According to blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis, compromised private keys accounted for 43.8% of cryptocurrency stolen in 2024 . Separately, DeFiLlama data showed that as of June of this year, blockchain projects have lost a cumulative $16.69 billion to hacks and exploits, with roughly 40% of those losses attributed to private-key compromises.

Recent examples include stablecoin protocol Resolv, which suffered a March attack involving a compromised private key controlling a privileged account and weaknesses in its minting system, allowing a hacker to extract about $25 million . In June, attackers compromised the private keys of a Humanity Protocol foundation member and drained more than $32 million from at least 17 wallets. The breach also sent the project's token plunging more than 80%, showing how stolen credentials can cause losses beyond the assets directly taken.

The tech giant's new system aims to reduce the risk of relying on a single private key by using "multi-party computation," or MPC, which distributes control of a private key among multiple parties or computers. This way, instead of relying on a single key, the system requires several distinct pieces of cryptographic information to work together to authorize a transaction.

The complete private key is never stored in one place, according to Google, reducing the risk of an attacker taking control of the assets, even if a single machine is compromised. It also said that customers retain control of their key material and that the company cannot access it in unencrypted form, even when key shares are held on Google's infrastructure.

Google is also positioning the service as a response to increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks, including threats involving artificial intelligence (AI) and quantum computing.

AI is already helping some cryptocurrency scammers operate on a larger scale, while researchers warn of potential future threats to the cryptography that protects digital assets.

Chainalysis found that cryptocurrency scams linked to AI-tool vendors extracted an average of $3.2 million per operation in 2025, compared with $719,000 for scams without such links — roughly 4.5 times as much. The findings suggest that AI may be helping fraudsters operate at a greater scale, although the report doesn't establish that AI directly caused the higher proceeds.

Recently, Ethereum researcher Justin Drake warned that advances in AI could eventually uncover mathematical shortcuts that could break the digital signatures protecting Bitcoin and Ethereum wallets. Drake said such a breakthrough could emerge in a worst-case scenario within months rather than years, potentially before sufficiently powerful quantum computers arrive.

No AI system has demonstrated the ability to break the cryptographic signatures that protect Bitcoin or Ethereum wallets. AI systems can be used to uncover flaws in poorly encrypted tools, such as last week's certification authority debacle. Google's current MPC protections address threats such as compromised credentials and unauthorized transactions, rather than a hypothetical breakthrough against the underlying cryptography.

The system can help address existing threats by checking transactions against institutional rules before they are signed, potentially preventing transfers that violate preset limits or approval requirements. Those controls may reduce the risk of unauthorized transactions . However, the risk of legitimate users being deceived into authorizing malicious transactions may still pose a threat.

Quantum computing, although not imminent, poses a distinct, longer-term threat to institutions exploring digital asset adoption.

Google researchers have previously estimated that a sufficiently powerful future quantum computer could theoretically derive a bitcoin private key from an exposed public key in roughly 9 minutes , assuming advanced preparation. While no quantum computer is currently capable of such an attack, about 6.9 million bitcoin have been reported as potentially vulnerable to future quantum attacks because their public keys have been exposed.

Google said its architecture is designed to support future upgrades to post-quantum cryptography, which seeks to protect digital signatures against attacks by sufficiently powerful quantum computers. The company said its MPC offering is designed to support conventional ECDSA and Ed25519 cryptographic signing algorithms at general availability.

Google did not provide a timetable for adding post-quantum signing capabilities but said the upgrades could be introduced as blockchain networks adopt the necessary cryptography, without requiring institutions to redesign their systems or interrupt operations.

A bank, for example, could keep one share of a cryptographic signing key in Google Cloud, another on its own hardware and a third with another cloud provider.

When the bank wants to move assets, the transaction enters Google's Confidential Space, where a policy engine checks it against the institution's rules before signing can begin, according to Google.

Those rules could include limits on the amount being transferred, restrictions on destination wallets and requirements for approval from several departments. The checks run inside Google's Confidential Space technology, which uses hardware-isolated computing environments designed to protect sensitive information from unauthorized access.

Google says the system can also accommodate different cryptographic signing thresholds, such as requiring two of three or five of seven participants to jointly produce a transaction signature.

That flexibility is intended to address a concern for banks: they may want the convenience of cloud infrastructure without giving a single technology provider complete control over the credentials needed to move their assets.

Google said institutions can distribute those credentials across their own hardware, Google Cloud and competing cloud services. The company also said its system supports fast transaction signing and key recovery, although it did not provide independently verified performance comparisons with existing custody products.

Google's planned entry to the market brings one of the world's largest cloud providers closer to competing in a market already served by specialist crypto security firms, including Fireblocks, Fordefi and BitGo, which offer technology to help institutions protect and authorize blockchain transactions.

Google argues that its banking relationships and security expertise give it an edge over specialized crypto custody providers. It also sees an opportunity among banks wary of relying on providers that compete for the same customers, positioning itself as a neutral infrastructure supplier that lets institutions run their own custody businesses.
